audits.name: Positive (ADM) mass theorem (Schoen-Yau 1979/1981, Witten 1981), inequality and rigidity clauses. The tree invokes it as 'never in danger' because m(r) < 0 locally is compatible with M_ADM >= 0.

audits.published_statement: EHLS 1110.2087 Theorem 1: 'Let 3 <= n < 8 and let (M, g, k) be an n-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set that satisfies the dominant energy condition. Then E >= |P|.' History, p.2: 'In the time-symmetric case [k = 0], we have that P = 0 and the dominant energy condition becomes the assumption that the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative. [Schoen-Yau] proved the time-symmetric case in dimension three in two articles from 1979 and 1981 ... In 1981 ... the general case k != 0 in dimension three ... E >= 0 by solving Jang's equation. Later, E. Witten discovered a completely different proof that E >= |P| in dimension three.' Rigidity (Huang-Lee p.2): in the time-symmetric case, 'if E = 0, then (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean space'. For general data E = |P| implies E = |P| = 0: proved by Beig-Chrusciel in 1996 (3D, spin) and by Huang-Lee in 2020 (n <= 7; for n = 3 embedding in Minkowski also needs tr k = O(r^-s), s > 2).
published_hypotheses: n = 3 (Schoen-Yau, Witten; spin is automatic for orientable 3-manifolds); 3 <= n < 8 in EHLS
complete C^2_loc metric g, C^1_loc k, no boundary
asymptotic flatness of type (p,q,q0,alpha): (g - delta, k) in W^{2,p}_{-q} x W^{1,p}_{-1-q}, q in ((n-2)/2, n-2), mu and J decaying like r^{-n-q0}
dominant energy condition mu >= |J| on the slice, with mu = (1/2)(R_g - |k|^2 + (tr k)^2); for k = 0 this is R_g >= 0
E_ADM is a flux integral of the metric's fall-off (EHLS Def.3), not a field-equation quantity
the rigidity clause is a separate theorem (Schoen-Yau for k = 0; Beig-Chrusciel 1996; Huang-Lee 2020)
no empirical data enter

later_literature.what: Proves E >= |P| without spin for n < 8, and restates the 1979/1981 hypotheses exactly. Huang-Lee Remark 2.11 says an extra regularity hypothesis should be added to EHLS Thm 1. That narrows the regularity class of the higher-dimensional statement, not the 3D theorem the tree uses.

Rigidity for general data: DEC and E=|P| give E=|P|=0 (n<=7). For n=3, embedding in Minkowski needs tr k = O(r^-s) with s>2. For the tree's static data, the older Schoen-Yau equality case already suffices.

later_literature.ref: de Aguiar Alves, Landulfo, Arderucio Costa arXiv 2408.00154 (2024)
later_literature.what: GR admits static negative-mass stars that violate the DEC and NEC, which is the class the PMT is silent on. The authors find these stars dynamically unstable, and cite PSW + Borde for positivity under AANEC and the null generic condition.

Positivity of mass from null focusing and time delay (AANEC + null generic) instead of the DEC. A result of this kind could rule out a bare negative mass while saying nothing at M=0. Cameron fn.1 records that PSW was never published and has gaps in its time-delay estimates. His own rigorous version is for D>=4 only and has no M=0 result.

audits.lacked_data: The theorem takes no measured input. It is an implication from completeness, asymptotic flatness and the DEC to E >= |P|, with rigidity at equality. Later work added mathematics, not data: proofs without spin (EHLS 2016), proofs in all dimensions (Schoen-Yau 2017, named not read), general-data rigidity (Beig-Chrusciel 1996, Huang-Lee 2020), and an extra regularity hypothesis for the 2016 statement. None of this moves the smooth, static 3+1 case the tree uses, and the recomputation here (C1-C4) agrees with the source. The physical assumption the authors made without measuring it is the DEC, and quantum fields were already known to violate it (Casimir). That violation does not falsify the theorem. It puts a configuration outside the theorem's scope, and every configuration on this board is outside it, by the board's own account (certify.py section 2, overturn.py:212-213, concentric.py:51-53, pair.py:124-129). So M's hypothesis gets no support from this result. What is missing is not data the authors lacked but a hypothesis the tree drops at phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8. The literature is genuinely incomplete in one place: the averaged-condition positivity results meant to cover the quantum regime (PSW 1993) are unpublished and have a recorded gap, and the rigorous D>=4 version gives nothing at M=0. The tree does not cite that line of work.
audits.grade_evidence: The theorem as published stands: statement and hypotheses were read via EHLS and Huang-Lee, the re-derivation agrees (C1-C4), and no datum enters. It is graded NARROWED because the tree applies it beyond its class, in three places. (1) phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8 drop the DEC and treat negative ADM mass as forbidden outright. C2 exhibits complete, regular, AF static data with E_ADM < 0 and R_g < 0 that the theorem does not forbid; z3 C4(i) confirms the case is consistent; 2408.00154 p.4 says the same in print. This exclusion carries phase1's ranking and the_winner(). (2) The 'never in danger / nothing to object to' uses (certify.py:161-164, overturn.py:217 and 679-680, concentric.py:49-50 and 271-273) are true but vacuous, because every configuration on the board violates the DEC. So they cannot tell the concentric corridor from a bare negative mass (C4 ii, iv, v). (3) phase1.py:195-197 and 537-539 ('no energy condition violated with M_ADM = 0') are contradicted by the rigidity clause for static, complete, compactly supported configurations. This is pair.py's own argument, and C3 computes R_g(0) = -2.9994e4. The rigidity uses themselves (concentric.py:51-53, pair.py:124-129) are valid (C4 iii). The grade is not WRONG, because nothing refutes the theorem. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no datum enters.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To reach STANDS, both of these are needed. First, phase1.py:397-399 and concentric.py:7-8 make the bare-negative-mass exclusion conditional on the DEC, or re-ground it on a result that holds without the DEC. A PSW-type theorem under AANEC + null generic rules out M<0 but is silent at M=0; it would have to be read at source, and its 3+1 status is contested (Cameron fn.1), so citing it would make that sub-claim OPEN, not STANDS. Second, phase1.py:195-197/537-539 adopt pair.py's reading ('satisfies the conclusion while violating the hypothesis'). WRONG would need a complete, AF, DEC-satisfying initial data set with E < |P|, contradicting EHLS Thm 1; nothing read here suggests one exists. OPEN would follow if the static (K=0) reading of phase1's configurations were withdrawn: drift item 3 would then have to be re-posed for k != 0 data via Huang-Lee Corollary 4.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: re-run script_path, check its encoding against the published statement, run the vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/pmt.py and ran it. It prints OVERALL OK and exits 0. Every printed number matches the audit: R(0) = -2.999400e4, core integral of R = -0.2318, m(R) = 39.7935069, Phi(1000) = -1.000e-15, and the docstring pair -6.250e-13 / 4.4471e-3 at a = 0.5.

Encoding against the source:
(a) C1 uses the EHLS Def.3 flux normalisation for n = 3, 1/(16 pi). It reproduces E = M for isotropic Schwarzschild. For the concentric slice, r^2 Phi' goes to 0, so E = 0.
(b) C3 checks the tree's actual metric. concentric.py:163-166 and composite.py:136-137 give g_ij = (1-2Phi) delta_ij, and I confirmed A_CORE = 0.02 and R_SHELL = 200 at lines 155-156. The R formula is checked symbolically for a generic Phi.
(c) The cited tree sites say what the audit says: phase1.py:195-197, 397-399 and 537-539, concentric.py:7-8 and 49-53, pair.py:103-129.

Vacuity guard (vguard.py V1): C4 is propositional. It checks the logic of the tree's uses of the theorem, not the theorem's content, and the report should say so plainly. But it is not vacuous. With the PMT premise removed, (ii) and (iii) become invalid. PMT & H & E<0 is UNSAT. With the hypothesis negated inside the encoding, (ii) no longer follows. PMT & H is satisfiable.

A finite check of the theorem itself was possible, and I ran one (V4). In the tree's own class (spherically symmetric, K = 0 slices), R = 4m'/r^2. So R >= 0 with m(0) = 0 gives M >= 0, and M = 0 forces a flat slice; this is the elementary spherical PMT together with its rigidity case. On the seated concentric slice the areal radius is monotone, so the argument applies. The Misner-Sharp mass is 0 at the centre, dips to -5.13e-3 at r = 0.15, and is 0 at infinity, so R < 0 somewhere. This agrees with C3 and with the audit's drift item 3 by a route that does not use z3.

Two encoding flaws, neither of which moves the grade:
(1) C2's constant-density ball has a step in rho. That makes g only Lipschitz at r = R, below the C^2_loc hypothesis the audit itself lists, so as coded C2 is not strictly admissible EHLS data. V3 redoes it with a smooth Gaussian density. The result holds: m(r) <= 0, M = -pi^(3/2) rho0 w^3 < 0, R = 16 pi rho < 0 everywhere, no horizon, regular centre. So the C2 conclusion stands.
(2) C1b and the data row say the first (wrong) potential gives ADM energy 'exactly -m'. That potential gives psi -> 1 + 2m/R_s, not 1, so the slice is not asymptotic to delta. Once it is normalised (x' = sqrt(c) x), E = -m/sqrt(1+2m/R_s), a factor of 0.999975 at the seated values. The sign and the conclusion are unchanged. This is a data-row overstatement: it narrows the row and should be recorded, not repaired.

The theorem's content is READ via EHLS and Huang-Lee, not machine-checked here. What the checks establish is that the tree applies the theorem beyond its class, which is exactly the NARROWED case.

What reproduces: I reran the rederivation script and got OVERALL OK, exit 0. I also recomputed the key numbers by hand.
- The row "empirical inputs = none" is correct. The PMT is an implication from completeness, asymptotic flatness and the DEC to E >= |P|, so no measured quantity enters.
- overturn.py: m(R) = (4/3)pi(9.5) = 39.7935069 and m(r0) = -4.1887902, matching overturn.py:181-183. max 2m/r is reached at r = R = 2 and equals 39.79, so rho must be scaled by less than 0.02513 for a static reading. The audit is right to call this a scale note, since overturn's conclusion is linear in rho.
- concentric.py at the seated a = 0.02, R_s = 200, m = 5e-3: Phi(1) = 4.97400e-3 against a selftest target of 4.9750e-3 with tolerance 1e-6, so it passes by about 3e-10. Phi(1000) = -1.000e-15.
- The docstring pair -6.2e-13 and +4.4e-3 is reproduced exactly by a = 0.5 (-6.250e-13 and 4.4471e-3). The stale-parameter discrepancy the audit records is real.
- bad(1000) = -2.0000e-5, as the audit says.
- Every "moves_conclusion: no" follows. M_ADM = 0 does not depend on a, and each residual is the a^2/r^3 Plummer tail, not a 1/r mass.

Inaccuracy 1, an unrecorded discrepancy: the pair.py residual row is incomplete.
- pair.py's prose at lines 123 and 510 says "measured at -4.000e-15".
- pair.py's own code at line 426 measures concentric.adm_residual(5.0e-3), which gives -1.000e-15 at the seated parameters.
- The audit attributes -4.000e-15 to m = 2e-2. That attribution is an inference and not unique: a = 0.04 with m = 5e-3 gives the same value.
- So this is a second prose-versus-code discrepancy, of the same kind as the concentric docstring one, and the audit does not record it. It moves nothing.

Inaccuracy 2, overstated precision: C1b's "ADM flux gives exactly -m" for bad().
- That potential tends to psi -> 1 + 2m/R_s at infinity rather than 1.
- Once the asymptote is normalised, E = -m/sqrt(1 + 2m/R_s) = -4.999875e-3 at m = 5e-3, a relative difference of 2.5e-5.
- "Exactly" is overstated at order m/R_s. Negative ADM mass, the point of that row, is unaffected.

lacked_data: it answers M's hypothesis with evidence rather than by presumption. The PMT takes no measured input. Later changes were mathematical: proofs without spin, all dimensions, general-data rigidity, and an extra regularity hypothesis. The gap it identifies is a hypothesis the tree drops, not data the authors lacked. That is backed by the computed checks C2 (a negative-mass ball that the theorem does not forbid) and C4 (z3). It also names one place where the literature really is incomplete: the PSW averaged-condition positivity result is unpublished and has a recorded gap. So "no support for M's hypothesis from this result" is argued with evidence.

Limitation: I could not re-read the cited literature at source in this pass. The alphaXiv quota was exceeded and the proxy returned 403 on arxiv.org. The citations 2408.00154 p.4, Cameron fn.1 and Huang-Lee Remark 2.11 are therefore unverified by me, not refuted. The grade does not hinge on them, because C2 and C4 carry the NARROWED finding computationally.

NARROWED is the grade the data evidence supports. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, since no datum enters, and not WRONG, since nothing refutes the theorem.

H2: G is the weighted mean of 16 input data that are mutually inconsistent, computed separately from every other constant. Every input uncertainty is expanded by a factor of 3.9 so that all normalized residuals are <= 2, and the quoted u_r of 2.2e-5 is that EXPANDED uncertainty (2409.03787 Secs. I.B.11, XIV, XV.A).

H5: the constants other than G come from one self-consistent least-squares adjustment, so E_h = alpha^2 m_e c^2 = 2hcR_inf and a_0 = hbar/(alpha m_e c).

audits.lacked_data: The evidence runs both ways. FOR M's hypothesis: CODATA 2018 did not have the Morel et al. 2020 h/m(87Rb) measurement. With it, CODATA 2022 moved alpha, and with it mu_0, eps_0, a_0 and m_e, by about 4.5 of their own 2018 standard uncertainties. For the four EM constants the tree seats, the 2018 values really did lack a datum that later moved them well outside 1 sigma. AGAINST it mattering here: those moves are 6.8e-10 to 1.36e-9 relative, at most 2.7e-9 on any tree formula, and the sandbox with the 2022 values flips no tolman, spec or drivensource check. For G it is the reverse of missing data. No new G datum arrived between 2018 and 2022. The problem is that 16 existing inputs disagree (residuals up to 7.75, expansion factor 3.9), and reanalyses of the same data dispute the value at ~5e-5 and the uncertainty by up to about 10x. Anywhere within the full span of the 16 inputs, no refusal verdict moves; order-level figures move by at most 1.6e-4 orders. What does move is the tree's quoted precision: its 6 to 11 s.f. pins fail at CODATA's own 1 sigma. Moving even a one-order figure would need G to be wrong by more than a factor of 10, and nothing read here suggests that.

verifiers.reason:
I tried to overturn NARROWED in both directions and could not.

**Source, read by me.** I read arXiv:2409.03787 myself through alphaXiv, pp.1-2, 50-51 and 60-64.
- Table XXXII/XXXIII give G = 6.674 30(15)e-11 with u_r 2.2e-5. They list hbar as '1.054 571 817 ...' and exact. l_P = 1.616 255(18)e-35, and the Planck energy is 1.220 890(14)e19 GeV.
- The 2022 EM values match the audit: mu_0 1.256 637 061 27(20)e-6, eps_0 8.854 187 8188(14)e-12, m_e 9.109 383 7139(28)e-31, a_0 5.291 772 105 44(82)e-11, E_h 4.359 744 722 2060(48)e-18.
- Sec. XVI.A says G's 2022 value is 'identical' to 2018. Sec. XVI.B.3 says there is no new G datum. Sec. XVI.C.2 gives the 3.9 expansion over 16 inputs, with largest residuals 7.7, 6.8 and 4.8 (BIPM-14, JILA-18, BIPM-01). Sec. XVI.C.1 attributes the alpha move to Morel et al. 2020.
- Table XXXVIII gives D_r = -4.5 for mu_0 and a_0, +4.5 for eps_0 and m_e, and -0.3 for R_inf and E_h. The caption defines D_r against u(2018) and says 'calculations were performed with extra digits'.

**NIST 2018 values.** The scipy 1.17.1 txt2018 lines for G, mu_0, eps_0, m_e, a_0, E_h, l_P and hbar match the audit exactly.

**The audit's numbers reproduce.**
- The typed HBAR is h/2pi truncated, -6.13e-10 relative.
- The derived l_P sits 1.51e-8 from the table value with exact hbar, and 1.48e-8 with the truncated hbar. G enters as an exact decimal, so the audit's WORDING discrepancy at tolman.py:2773-2774 stands.
- mu_0 gives D_r = -4.47.
- Across the 16 inputs, G spans -3.58e-4 relative (LENS-14) to +1.86e-4 (BIPM-01). That is at most 1.56e-4 orders, which matches 'at most 1.6e-4 orders' and '3.6e-4 relative'.
- At +1 sigma G, ledger.py:3033-3034's 7-figure check (round(rate/1e26,6) == 1.348948) becomes 1.348917 and fails, as claimed.

**The E_h/R_inf D_r point is real, and it stays unadjudicated.** From the printed values, E_h's D_r is -0.13 against u(2018) and -0.23 against u(2022). R_inf's is -0.14 and -0.25. Rounding of the last digit can move these by only about ±0.05, so extra digits cannot produce -0.3 for E_h on the caption's own definition. That is a discrepancy in the restatement, it touches no tree figure, and the audit rightly neither calls it an error nor rests the grade on it.

**Refuting toward STANDS fails.**
- The rubric counts 'a hypothesis the tree drops' as NARROWED, and the drop is real. Nine G sites type a bare point value with no u_r.
- The tree uses G-dependent figures as physical values, not only as regression pins. index3.py:1719 quotes ledger row D11 as 'MEASURED at 1.348948e+26 kg per metre', 7 s.f. on an input CODATA gives to 2.2e-5. higgs.py:637 pins xi_required, which scales as 1/G, at 1e-9.
- The tree's own hierarchy.py:162-167 carries G_REL, which shows the hypothesis can be kept.

**Refuting toward DATA-DEPENDENT or WRONG fails.** The EM values did move (+/-4.5 u, which bears out M's missing-data hypothesis for them), and G's consensus is contested at about 5e-5. But no datum moves a verdict: order-level figures move by at most 1.6e-4 orders, and the EM shifts are about 1e-9. Nothing refutes the values, and the truncated HBAR is a digits discrepancy, not WRONG.

**One overstatement, which does not move the grade.** Two items on the audit's list of over-precise pins are softer than it implies:
- higgs.py:609's Planck mass 1.220890e19 is CODATA's own printed figure to the same digits. Only its 1e-5 tolerance is slightly tighter than u_r 1.1e-5.
- seatindex's 9.50536e43 is checked at 1e-5 relative, against G's 2.2e-5.
ledger.py:3033 and higgs.py:637 still carry the narrowing on their own.

The 2018 RMP paper itself is NAMED-NOT-READ, which the audit discloses. The values it relies on were read in the NIST table and corroborated by the 2022 successor, so that does not weaken the grade.

audits.published_statement:
Abstract (p.1): 'In flat space, the covariant entropy bound reduces to the Bekenstein bound. The latter does not contain Newton's constant and cannot operate via gravitational backreaction.'

Sec 2.2 (p.5): 'In its original form, the bound states that the entropy S of any weakly gravitating matter system obeys S <= 2 pi M R/hbar, (2.2) where M is the total gravitating mass of the matter and R is the radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system. The absence of Newton's constant in Bekenstein's bound is notable. It renders Eq. (2.2) independent of the strength of gravity, G, in its regime of validity. In particular, the bound remains nontrivial when gravity is turned off completely (G = 0).'

Weak-gravity condition, eq (2.3): M << R/G.

Sec 2.1 (p.4): the covariant bound A/4G hbar becomes 'more lenient as G -> 0, and trivial for G = 0'.

Eq (3.2): S <~ M R/(l_Pl^2/G), which 'involves only the combination l_Pl^2/G'.

p.8: 'our understanding of the Bekenstein bound is still imperfect... quite sensitive to the precise definition of the entropy'.

p.10: an example that precisely saturates the bound 'is an important outstanding problem.'
published_hypotheses: H1 WEAKLY GRAVITATING matter system, M << R/G (eq 2.3). The G-independence is asserted 'in its regime of validity' (p.5), and the derivation 'applies only in weakly gravitating regions' (p.3).
H2 M is the total gravitating mass and R is the radius of the smallest sphere that barely fits around the system (p.5).
H3 hbar is the constant held fixed. The source writes the bound in hbar-form (2.2). In its own axiomatic form (3.2), with l_Pl primitive, the bound reads S <~ M R G/l_Pl^2.

H5 Entropy is the log of the number of Fock-space states compatible with the boundary conditions (p.2). The source says the bound is sensitive to how entropy is defined and assumes a rigorous formulation exists (p.8).

H6 (derivation only, not the quoted claim) The generalized covariant entropy bound is taken as an axiom. Sec 3 is a simplified argument good to factors of order one; the rigorous derivation is ref [17], hep-th/0210295.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1 (weakly gravitating, 'in its regime of validity'). bounds.py:309-312 quotes the two phrases without this qualifier, and the canonical entry's only hypothesis is 'S <= 2 pi R E'. DOCKET.md:193-195 does the same. The quotes themselves are verbatim.

TWO REGIMES MIXED IN ONE ROW. The same row codes black-hole saturation: bounds.py:312-313 ('the black-hole SATURATION ... already carried by K = 0'), bounds.py:315 ('saturated by black holes') and DOCKET.md:196-201 (argument 3). A Schwarzschild hole has M/(R/G) = 1/2 (computed), which is outside regime (2.3). At G = 0, where 'remains nontrivial' is asserted, no black hole exists. Inside the regime, the source calls a precisely saturating example 'an important outstanding problem' (p.10). This bears on why K = 0 was chosen, which is a different key. It does not bear on the G coordinate.

H3 (hbar held fixed) IS NOT STATED. The tree's G rule is a syntactic test on the statement (bounds.py:27, bounds.py:309-310, DOCKET.md:189-191). In the source's own form (3.2), G appears. With l_Pl held fixed, the limit G -> 0 sends the bound to 0 (rederive checks f and f'). The tree's quote is faithful to the hbar-form; the drift is that the tree does not name that form as the hypothesis.

DROPPED CAVEAT H5. The source says the bound's formulation is unsettled: entropy definition and the species problem (p.8). bounds.py:315 seats 'Bekenstein' as a definite bound with K = 0. The tree seats Casini's rigorous form separately, at bounds.py:305-307.
NO DRIFT between S <= 2 pi R E and 2 pi M R/hbar: they are the same at c = hbar = 1.

rederivation.outcome:
All 12 checks agree with the source.
(a) dS_Bek/dG = 0 in hbar-form, and the bound is nonzero at G = 0.
(b) A/4G hbar -> infinity as G -> 0.
(c) S_Bek/S_hol = 2GM/R exactly, so the Bekenstein bound is tighter exactly when M << R/G.
(d) A Schwarzschild hole (R = 2GM) saturates 2 pi M R/hbar exactly, but its M/(R/G) = 1/2 puts it outside the stated regime.
(e) 2GM -> 0 as G -> 0.
(f) In the l_Pl-form, S = 2 pi G M R/l_Pl^2: G appears, and the G -> 0 limit is 0.
(g) The X-ray argument (deflection 4GM/R, lever arm R) reproduces 2 pi M R/hbar. The lever arm is an order-one choice made here.
(h) For the electron, the holographic figure computes to 1.8e45 to 7.1e46 against the printed 10^44. This is a discrepancy, not an error.

later_literature.what: Proves a flat-space QFT version of the bound, S_V - S_V^0 <= K_V - K_V^0, as positivity of relative entropy. It contains no G and has no species problem, so 'nontrivial with gravity off' becomes a theorem for this version. It also supports H1: relative entropy 'becomes ill defined once the backreaction is included ... the static limit is crucial, what means a flat space limit' (p.8). And it says there is 'no general consensus on the correct value of lambda or the meaning of R' (p.3).

States lambda as 'some order-one constant independent of G_N' and calls Casini's version a widely accepted proven form. It narrows a reading the tree does not use: that the bound limits information in general (zero-bits escape it when only the decoder is restricted).
The rigorous derivation from the generalized covariant bound, for weakly gravitating systems.
The original bound, derived from the generalized second law with a black-hole thought experiment.

audits.lacked_data: The claim is about which constants appear in eq (2.2), so no measured datum enters and nothing was missing in that sense. What came later is theory. Casini (2008) supplied the rigorous flat-space formulation that Bousso said was missing (p.8). It contains no G and is proven with gravity absent, so it confirms the conclusion. It also confirms the hypothesis the tree drops: it needs a fixed, flat-limit geometry. The electron example is off by 1.3 to 2.9 orders of magnitude, but the constants behind it have not moved (G is the same in 2018 and 2022; hbar is exact since 2019). So the gap is not caused by missing data, and it does not touch the claim. On M's hypothesis for this result, no evidence supports it, and the later rigorous work makes the result stronger.

The claim the tree actually uses is that S <= 2 pi R E contains no G, so G = 0 under the rule at bounds.py:27. That holds in the form the source states. The pins that rest on it pass and do not move: bounds.py:459, 469, 528 and 538-539.

The grade is NARROWED because the tree drops two qualifiers the source attaches: 'in its regime of validity' for 'any weakly gravitating matter system' (M << R/G), and the hbar-form (bounds.py:309-312; DOCKET.md:193-195).

The dropped regime matters inside the same row. The tree pairs the G-free quote with black-hole saturation (bounds.py:312-315; DOCKET.md:196-201). A black hole has M/(R/G) = 1/2, is outside that regime, and does not exist at G = 0. Inside the regime, the source calls a precisely saturating example an outstanding problem (p.10). That affects why K = 0 was chosen, which is a different key.

It is not WRONG: no contradiction was found. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
It would become STANDS if the tree named 'weakly gravitating, M << R/G, hbar-form' next to the quote and in the canonical entry, and either stopped using black-hole saturation to support K = 0 or named it as a strong-gravity fact outside Bousso's regime (for example by citing Casini's asymptotic flat-space saturation, eqs 43-44).

It would become WRONG only if hbar-form (2.2) were shown to contain G, or to become trivial at G = 0 with hbar fixed. The checks here show the opposite.

COMPUTATIONS. I re-ran the auditor's script and every check passes. I recomputed the key ones independently:
- S_Bek/S_hol = 2GM/R.
- A Schwarzschild hole has GM/R = 1/2.

The STANDS direction was my strongest attempt. The tree's G slot is a syntactic test on the statement. At G = 0, GM/R = 0, so every system is inside regime (2.3). Dropping the weak-gravity qualifier therefore cannot by itself overturn the G = 0 use, and the auditor concedes this.

That attempt fails on the hbar-form hypothesis, which is real and moves the integer. In the source's own l_P-primitive form (3.2), the Bekenstein bound contains G: S <~ G M R/l_P^2. The covariant bound becomes pi R^2/l_P^2, which has no G but still has an area, so it stays G = 1. Under the tree's own rule ('a G or an area appears'), Bekenstein's G integer therefore depends on which constant is held primitive. The source itself says the bound 'involves only the combination l_Pl^2/G'. The tree names neither this hypothesis nor the regime of validity: the canonical entry's only hypothesis is 'S <= 2 pi R E'. The same justification also cites black-hole saturation (bounds.py:312-313), which lies outside Bousso's stated domain. A hypothesis that is unnamed and convention-dependent, and on which a pinned integer rests, is a narrowing. It is not STANDS.

The WRONG and DATA-DEPENDENT directions also fail. No contradiction exists, and no measured datum enters the claim.

One overstatement, recorded as a discrepancy and not a grade change. The auditor gives the electron example as off by '1.3 to 2.9 orders'. The upper end uses R = h/(m_e c), but the source sets R ≈ hbar/M (p.5), so only the reduced-Compton figure is the source's own input:

- Without the pi, at order-of-magnitude level, R^2/l_P^2 = 5.71e44, which is 0.76 decades above.

The discrepancy is therefore about 0.8 to 1.3 decades, not up to 2.9. This makes the auditor's 'discrepancy, not error' reading stronger. The tree does not use the electron figure.

I did not check the later-literature summaries (Casini 0804.2182, Hayden-Wang 2309.07436). They do not bear on the grade.

audits.published_statement:
Wang's restatement (1206.5618, p.2): 'Assume that Theta^{mu nu}(x) is a Lorentz four-tensor given in the laboratory frame ..., Theta is independent of time, and further Theta^{i4}(x) = 0 ... von Laue's theorem [1] states: The time-row-element space integrals P^mu = int_V Theta^{mu 4} d^3x constitute a Lorentz four-vector if and only if int_V Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 (2).' Wang fn.7 adds: 'In the original ref. 1, Laue only gave the proof that int Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 is a sufficient condition.'

The finite-volume relation the tree cites is Wang sec.6, eq.(20). It comes from the three-dimensional Gauss law: oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V (d_l Theta^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + int_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x. On p.5 Wang says 'divergence-less plus an additional boundary condition can be a sufficient condition ... oint_S dS_l Theta^{l mu} X^i = 0 holds, which is true if Theta = 0 is imposed on the boundary', and that divergence-less alone 'is neither a necessary condition nor a sufficient condition'.

Pinto & Avelino (eqs.(24)-(25)) give the modern vanishing form: 'If T^{mu j} = 0 at dSigma or if Sigma represents the whole fixed time hyperplane and T^{mu j} decays sufficiently fast (e.g. ~1/r^{3+eps}) then int_Sigma T^{mu i} d^3x = 0.' Lorce et al. eq.(15) states it for a closed system as 'the von Laue condition for mechanical equilibrium int d^3x p(x) = 0', with surface terms dropped by assumption.
published_hypotheses: static: dTheta^{mu nu}/dt = 0 in the frame considered (Wang sec.2, emphasised on p.3)
Theta^{i4} = 0 for the classical four-vector form (Wang sec.2)
closed system: the TOTAL stress-energy tensor is divergence-free and there is no external force density (Lorce eqs.(14),(19)); with a force density F, int T^{ij} = -int x^i F^j (Lorce eq.(18))

boundary condition: T^{l mu} = 0 on the bounding surface (Wang p.5; Pinto-Avelino eq.(25); Sorge assumption (a) and eq.(35)), OR integration over all space with T decaying faster than 1/r^3 (Pinto-Avelino eq.(25))
divergence-free alone is NOT sufficient: the field-only EM tensor of a charged sphere, or of a finite electrostatic structure, violates the condition (Wang secs.4-6)
flat (Minkowski) spacetime, i.e. negligible self-gravity (Pinto-Avelino p.1, sec.III)
the integrals converge (Wang eq.(1))

That needs T^{ij} n_j = 0 ON the enclosing sphere (compact support inside the ball). A bounded DEVICE is not enough, because its own static fields extend past it. In Wang, eq.(20) is his own sec.6 Gauss-law identity. Von Laue's theorem proper (sec.2) is the four-vector criterion, with int Theta^{ij} = 0 as its condition, and Wang fn.7 says Laue proved only sufficiency. The restatements disagree on this: Lorce et al. p.5 says von Laue showed the condition is necessary and sufficient. The mathematics the tree uses is unaffected either way.

later_literature.what: Divergence-free alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for int Theta^{ij} = 0. Divergence-free plus the boundary condition (Theta = 0 on the boundary) is sufficient. Counterexamples are a charged metal sphere and a finite electrostatic structure, using the field-only tensor. Wang's further claim, that the Landau-Lifshitz and Weinberg versions are 'flawed', concerns the four-vector theorem, not the part the tree uses.

QFT version for a closed system in a stationary state: <int T^ii> = 0 (eq.14) and <int T^ij> = 0 (eq.19), with surface terms dropped by assumption. With an external force, int T^ij = -int x^i F^j (eq.18). M = <int T^mu_mu> (eq.65). Attributes the necessary-and-sufficient form to von Laue, which conflicts with Wang fn.7.

For a Casimir apparatus in a weak field, int sqrt(-g) T^i_i = 0 (eq.36). This assumes T vanishes outside the domain (assumption (a)) and on its boundary (eq.(35)), with ideal plates and edge effects neglected.

audits.lacked_data:
In 1911 von Laue did not have GR (1915), QFT with renormalised vacuum stress (Casimir, 1948), or hadron pressure data (gravitational form factors, from 2018). The sources read here show that having them does not change the conclusion:
(i) The finite-volume relation is a pure identity with no empirical input; it is re-derived here in C1 and C2.
(ii) The vanishing form carries over to QFT stationary states (Lorce et al. eqs.14 and 19) and to a Casimir apparatus to first order in a weak field (Sorge eq.36). No refutation was found or constructed.
(iii) The only limit later work makes explicit is a hypothesis that was always needed, not new data: the boundary term must vanish (Moller's zero-boundary condition, 1955, as reported by Wang; Pinto-Avelino eq.25). Pinto & Avelino 2025 quantify how large the finite-ball deviation can be.
Hadron data do not test the condition: the proton analyses assume it. Whether any measurement has been independent of it was NOT checked here.
M's hypothesis is not supported for this result; no datum has moved.
audits.grade_evidence:
What stands: the identity the tree cites, Wang eq.(20), re-derives exactly (C1 symbolic; C2 sympy residual 0 on a non-spherical conserved stress). Its direction as the tree now states it is confirmed: the surface term is on the left and equals 4 pi R^3 <T^rr>.

What is narrowed: the vanishing form holds on a smaller class than tolman.py:1015-1017 and 2622-2625 state. It needs T = 0 on the enclosing sphere (compact support), which Wang, Sorge and Pinto & Avelino all state. 'Complete static bounded system' is not enough when the device's fields extend past it. Computed counterexample (C3d): a bounded device with a conserved complete tensor gives int_{ball R} T^ii = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R), nonzero on every finite enclosing ball. Pinto & Avelino 2025 bound the same deviation in general, and C3h reproduces their bound exactly.

Why no verdict moves: the code already carries the hypothesis. z3 L1 (tolman.py:2387-2405) takes p_r = 0 at the cut as a premise, and DRIFT L2 proves it load-bearing, so the narrowing is in prose only. The refusal 'ball_excludes_walls' stays conservative under the narrower class: it may refuse where the test had content, but it never reports a false zero.

What is not a refutation: the attribution of eq.(20) to von Laue, the 35 versus 340 volume number, and 'eq.(20) needs a ball' are discrepancies.

Why this grade: not STANDS, because the printed statement drops a required hypothesis and a counterexample to it is computed here. Not WRONG, because the result as the tree applies it (L1) is correct.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS: tolman.py:1015-1017 and 2622-2625 would need to say that the boundary of the ball lies outside the support of the complete T, or define 'bounded system' as compact support of T, so that the prose matches L1. That is a change to the tree, which this audit does not make.
On the attribution alone: reading von Laue 1911 at source would settle whether Laue proved sufficiency only (Wang fn.7) or the necessary-and-sufficient form (Lorce et al. p.5). That cannot be done here, since there is no arXiv copy, and either answer leaves the mathematics unchanged.
To WRONG: the tree would have to apply the vanishing form to a T that is not compactly supported inside the ball. No such application was found.

The form the tree uses, Wang 1206.5618 p.5 eq.(20): 'from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law we have oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = INT_V (d_l Theta^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + INT_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x'; p.2 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected'.
published_hypotheses: F (here W^l = T^{lj} x^i) is C^1 on the closure of the region (classical, Chen-Torres p.1, p.3). Weakened forms: Lipschitz (De Giorgi-Federer, p.5); Sobolev/BV on Lipschitz domains (p.5); divergence-measure fields DM^p, with the formula as a limit over interior smooth approximations (Chen-Comi-Torres Thms 2-3, pp.9-10)

The divergence is taken over the WHOLE region. A singular point of F inside the region carries its own contribution: Whitney's example (p.8) has div F = 0 pointwise in the open square, yet the boundary flux is pi/2

The region is bounded, with piecewise smooth / C^1 / Lipschitz / finite-perimeter boundary. Multiply connected regions are allowed, and every boundary component contributes (Wang p.2, p.4; Ruf Thm 1.1)
Flat Euclidean 3-space with Cartesian x^i in Wang eq.(20)
The theorem itself says nothing about div F = 0 or about any boundary term vanishing. Wang eq.(20) keeps both terms, and zeroing either is an extra physical hypothesis (Wang p.5)

The tree's own independence_witness (tolman.py:1381-1388) is divergence-free at every point of the punctured ball, yet int_B T^ii = 0 vs 4 pi R^3 <T^rr> = 4 pi A. The shell form is exact, and the distributional divergence at the origin is -4 pi A (rederive D5). This is the 3-D analogue of Whitney's example (D6). Family F's LAUE (tolman.py:2196-2198) bakes the hypothesis in: LAUE excludes the witness (z3 D8a unsat) and LAUE plus C admits it (D8b sat). The mutation table at :886-905 names only axisymmetry for F. The drop is in prose and in F's encoding only; no verdict moves.

OVER-RESTRICTIVE in the canonical entry (not the tree's wording): 'smooth divergence-free tensor on a ball'. The tree's W3 (tolman.py:584) is not C^1 at the centre (W = T.x is unbounded), yet the identity holds with inner flux -> 0 (D4). NAMING (a discrepancy, not an error): 'Stokes's theorem' (:938) vs 'the divergence theorem' (:139). It is the Gauss-Ostrogradsky theorem, the n-dim case of the generalised Stokes theorem, so the name is conventional.

later_literature.what: Survey of extensions of the classical theorem: Lipschitz fields on finite-perimeter sets, BV fields, and divergence-measure fields with normal traces. Whitney's and Silhavy's examples mark the limits of the hypotheses; they are not counterexamples to the theorem.

later_literature.what: A divergence theorem with inner boundaries, which holds iff H^{m-1}(dU minus ext*U) < infinity. Every boundary component, inner ones included, contributes, which is the structure behind the tree's centre term C.

audits.lacked_data: This is a mathematical theorem, so there is no measured input its 19th-century authors lacked. What came later is analysis, not data. The regularity hypotheses were weakened (Lipschitz, BV, DM^p, rough domains, inner boundaries), which extends the theorem. Whitney-type counterexamples apply only to fields outside the hypotheses, with nonzero distributional divergence at a singular point. Nothing read here, and nothing in the discover_papers listing, contradicts the theorem within its hypotheses, so for this result M's hypothesis is NOT supported. The only missing input is on the tree's side: at the Laue sites (tolman.py:139, 937-939; LAUE at 2196-2198) the regularity input, C = 0 / a regular centre, is used without being named. The same file names it everywhere else, so the gap is a label, not data, and no conclusion moves.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE
verifiers.reason:
The audit's facts all check out. Its grade does not follow from them. FACTS CONFIRMED: I copied rederive/stokes-divergence-theorem.py to verify/refute/stokes/ and ran it: ALL PASS, 21 checks, D1-D8 including the z3 pair and the vacuity guard. I read both sources myself through alphaXiv. Chen-Torres 2005.10949 p.3 eq.(1) says 'F is a C^1 vector field, E is a bounded open set with piecewise smooth boundary', and Whitney Example 2 on p.8 gives '0 = divF(E) != ... = pi/2'. Wang 1206.5618 p.5 eq.(20) is 'from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law', p.2 says 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected', and pp.4-5 say divergence-less is neither necessary nor sufficient without a boundary condition. All of these are quoted correctly. The independence witness is also right: it is conserved on the punctured ball, int T^ii = 0, and 4 pi R^3 p_r = 4 pi A.

WHY NARROWED DOES NOT HOLD. The docket's NARROWED means 'holds on a smaller class than the tree uses, or a hypothesis the tree drops'. Neither is the case. (1) The audit itself says THE EXTERNAL THEOREM STANDS, and that no F verdict or pointwise_test REPORT is ever issued on a source with C != 0. So the tree never applies the theorem outside its class. (2) The hypothesis as used in canonical.json is 'smooth divergence-free tensor on a ball'. That is stronger than the theorem needs (the audit's own D4), so the theorem holds on a LARGER class than the tree uses, which is the opposite of narrowed. (3) The citation at tolman.py:132 is Wang eq.(20) 'for a divergence-free time-independent tensor' on V = the ball. Eq.(20) is the classical C^1 divergence law (Chen-Torres eq.(1)), so a singular centre makes the field fail the cited theorem's own hypothesis. Line 139's 'NO INTEGRATION CONSTANT' is then true within that hypothesis, and citing a theorem does not oblige the tree to restate its hypotheses. (4) The tree does not drop regularity. It flags this exact case itself. tolman.py:1383-1386 says of the very witness the audit uses as its counterexample: 'C = 4 pi lim r^3 p_r = 4 pi A != 0 so THIS identity's hypothesis FAILS'. :302-304 tabulates 'regular centre dropped: ... 4 pi R^3 p_r + C'. Family D (:2129-2157) machine-checks 'REGULAR CENTRE IS NECESSARY' (D6) and 'C IS A GENUINE DEGREE OF FREEDOM' (DRIFT D2). :1198 and :2964-2967 enforce regular_centre in code. (5) Family F's LAUE is a premise, not a widening. :937-938 says 'Family F encodes the CONCLUSION of Wang eq. (20) as a constraint, not its proof'. A premise cannot extend a theorem's class: every F result is conditional on eq.(20) holding, and the condition that makes it hold is carried by family D. The families are deliberate slices, and F's mutation table naming only axisymmetry is consistent with that.

The audit's own route to STANDS is 'name the hypothesis at :139 and :937-939'. That route changes the tree's prose, not the external result, which shows the grade is grading a label. Under M's rule against over-representation in either direction, a regularity hypothesis that is stated in the same file, machine-checked in family D, and enforced in code should not be graded as a narrowing of Gauss-Ostrogradsky. The label gap at :937-939 (Stokes CITED with no hypothesis restated) and the 'Stokes'/'divergence theorem' naming are worth recording as discrepancies. They are not a dropped hypothesis. The proposed grade is STANDS: the theorem stands, its hypotheses as used sit inside it, the re-derivation agrees, and no datum enters.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the script, check that its encoding matches the published statement, and run the vacuity guard
verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN: I ran a copy of the audit script at verify/rederive/stokes-divergence-theorem.py. It reproduces ALL PASS: 21 checks, exit 0, about 9 s wall time against the claimed 3 s; that difference is immaterial. The line numbers it cites in tolman.py (139, 280-286, 567, 584, 886-905, 931-939, 1198, 1266-1273, 1381-1388, 2196-2198, 2964-2975) all read as the audit quotes them.

ENCODING: D2 is a single polynomial instance, not the theorem in general. It is the trace contraction on a ball for one div-free T = delta Lap(phi) - dd(phi). I closed that gap with my own vacuity_extra.py. V1 checks Gauss on the ball for a GENERAL cubic vector field with 60 symbolic coefficients, residual 0. V3 checks the full 9-component tensor form of Wang eq.(20), int T^{ij} = oint n_l T^{lj} x^i, on D2's T, residual 0. So what the script tests is the theorem in the form the tree uses it, not a toy of it. The D8 z3 layer is a re-encoding of LAUE, not the tree's own callable. It drops the I_Th conjunct, but I_Th is unconstrained there, so the omission is harmless. D8a and D8b reduce to the trivial algebra F*A = 0 with F > 0 and A != 0. They are correct but shallow, and the substantive evidence is in sympy D5.

VACUITY: with the hypothesis negated, the check fails as it should. V2 takes T = diag(x^2,0,0), which is not div-free: the trace identity gives 4piR^5/15 vs 4piR^5/5. V2b keeps Wang's div term and the identity is restored. V5 moves Whitney's singularity outside the closed square and the flux returns to 0 = int div. So D2, D5 and D6 discriminate rather than pass trivially. The D8c guard is also sat.

TWO MINOR DISCREPANCIES, neither of which moves the grade. (1) The audit calls -4piA 'the distributional divergence at the origin'. The script actually computes the pairing <T, grad(x g)> = -4piA, so with the usual convention <div T, phi> = -<T, grad phi> the divergence is +4piA. The sign is a matter of convention in the wording; the load-bearing claim is that it is nonzero, and that holds. (2) V4 shows the independence witness is not even locally integrable: |T^xx| has angular integral about 4.84 times log(1/eps), which diverges. It therefore lies outside even the divergence-measure (DM) hypotheses, and its 'distributional divergence' needs a principal-value reading beyond radial test fields. This strengthens the audit's point that the ball form fails because the theorem's hypothesis fails. It does not weaken it. D4 (W3 is not C^1, yet the inner flux goes to 0) and D7 (the Laplace-tension sign and magnitude) re-check by hand.

GRADE: the external theorem STANDS, as re-derived and generalised above. The tree's wording at :139 and :937-939, and the F-family LAUE conjunct, leave the regular-centre / C = 0 hypothesis unnamed. That hypothesis is carried elsewhere in the file (:280-286, :931-936, :1198, :2964-2967), and no verdict moves. NARROWED is supported.

The one data_at_publication row says no numerical input enters the theorem: value_then and value_now are both n/a, and moves_conclusion is no. That is right. The Gauss-Ostrogradsky theorem is a mathematical identity, with a proof under stated regularity hypotheses (C^1/Lipschitz field, bounded region with piecewise-smooth/Lipschitz boundary), and nothing is measured. The canonical entry agrees: its data_used is [] and its kind is theorem. The tree's use of it agrees too. tolman.py:129-139 'Strip gravity' takes flat-space Wang eq.(20) with no numerical input, and :937-939 cites Stokes with no data. The only numbers near the Laue step are the tree's own fixtures, F5/F6 (p_t=-5, p_z=+1, <T^rr>=-3, :567-572). Those are constructed witnesses, not external data, so 'no datum to move' follows.

The lacked_data answer settles M's hypothesis (earlier physicists lacked data) on evidence, not by assuming it. First, no data input exists for this result. Second, what came later is analysis that extends the regularity class: Chen-Torres 2005.10949 (READ by restatement) and Ruf 2506.09978 (READ). Whitney-type examples fall outside the hypotheses; they do not refute the theorem. Third, the re-derivation runs here: I ran the script myself and got ALL PASS, exit 0, with D6 (Whitney's example: div F=0, flux pi/2) and D8 (z3: LAUE excludes the witness, sat once C is added; vacuity guard sat). So 'M's hypothesis NOT supported for this result' is backed by evidence, and it stays scoped to this result.

The missing input it names is on the tree's side: the regular-centre condition C=0 is unlabelled at :139 and :937-939 and in LAUE at :2195-2198. That checks out against the source text. C appears as 'centre boundary term' at :280-286, refusal 3 names 'Regular centre' at :931-936, and independence_witness at :1381-1388 is described as conserved with C=4 pi A != 0. This is a hypothesis label the citing sites omit, not missing data, and correctly no conclusion moves. Nothing in the data lens overstates the result either way: the theorem is not called wrong and the tree is not called wrong.

One limit: the two later-literature items read at abstract level only (2410.09214, 2607.11467) are correctly marked not read and carry no weight. Grade NARROWED stands on the hypothesis-drift finding, which this lens neither strengthens nor weakens.

audits.lacked_data:
This entry is itself a record of earlier authors lacking data. Evidence both ways:

- RPP 2022's 125.25 lacked ATLAS's 2023 Run-2 combination (125.10 +- 0.11). With it, RPP 2024 moved to 125.20.
- RPP 2024/2025's 125.20 lacked CMS's 2024 four-lepton result (125.04 +- 0.12). With it, RPP 2026 moved to 125.13.
- RPP 2026 lacks CMS's July 2026 diphoton result (125.13 +- 0.15, arXiv:2607.28396). That result retires the 2016 value 125.78, which contributes 6.2 of the 6.9 chi2. A sensitivity average with the new result is 125.086 +- 0.068.

Every step moved toward the ATLAS/CMS cluster near 125.05-125.10. Each step stayed within 0.71 sigma of the previous edition's own error (0.29 and 0.64 sigma). So the old values were not wrong: each was a correct average of the data then available, with an honest error.

Having the later data changes nothing the tree concludes from these two numbers. W9(d) is an arithmetic identification of the input, and re-derivation confirms that only 125.25 fits the orchestrator's three figures. All figure shifts are at most 1.1e-3, and no verdict rests on that digit.

What the tree lacked runs the other way: it had not read the 2022 and 2024 listings. It therefore calls 125.20 NAMED-NOT-READ and leaves 125.25 unattributed, although both are READable PDG averages.

source.located: Primary: Schrodinger, Ann. Phys. 79 (1926) 361 (levels); <r>_{nl} via Waller Z. Phys. 38 (1926) 635 / Pasternack PNAS 23 (1937) 91 / Kramers 1938 -- none on arXiv. Read via restatement in: arXiv:0707.1887 (Suslov & Trey, J. Math. Phys. 49 (2008) 012104) p.8-11 eqs (3.1)-(3.5), (3.13)-(3.15), p.16 eqs (4.16)-(4.17); arXiv:0908.0032 (Cordero-Soto & Suslov 2009) p.2 eqs (2.6)-(2.7); arXiv:2409.03787 (CODATA 2022) p.10-11 eqs (26), (28)-(31), p.15 eq (50), Tables IV, XXXII, XXXIII.
source.via: Page text from alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries for all three arXiv papers, plus 1807.08337 and 2602.14980 for later literature. Schrodinger 1926, Waller 1926, Pasternack 1937 and Kramers 1938 are NAMED-NOT-READ. The formulas come from Suslov-Trey eqs (3.5) and (3.15). These agree with Cordero-Soto-Suslov eqs (2.6)-(2.7), with CODATA eq (26) at F = 0, and with excite.py:953-958.

audits.published_statement: Suslov & Trey (0707.1887 p.8-9): 'The nonrelativistic Coulomb wave functions ... psi_nlm = R_nl(r) Y_lm, R_nl = (2/n^2)(Z/a0)^{3/2} sqrt((n-l-1)!/(n+l)!) e^{-eta/2} eta^l L^{2l+1}_{n-l-1}(eta), eta = (2Z/n)(r/a0), a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2) ... n = 1,2,3,...; l = 0,1,...,n-1 ... The corresponding discrete energy levels in the cgs units are given by Bohr's formula E_n = -m Z^2 e^4/(2 hbar^2 n^2) (3.5) ... they do not depend on the quantum number of the orbital angular momenta l due to a hidden SO(4)-symmetry'; p.10: '<r> = (a0/2Z)(3n^2 - l(l+1)) (3.15)'. Cordero-Soto & Suslov (0908.0032 eqs 2.6-2.7): the Kramers-Pasternack recursion with '<1/r> = Z/(a0 n^2), <1> = 1'. CODATA 2022 (2409.03787 eq 26): 'E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1 + F) ... E_h = alpha^2 m_e c^2 ... F is small compared to one and is determined by QED, recoil corrections, etc.' Setting hbar = c = 1, e^2 = alpha and Z = 1 gives E_n = -m alpha^2/(2n^2), a0 = 1/(m alpha) and <r> = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m alpha). This is exactly excite.py:954-958.

audits.lacked_data:
What Schrodinger lacked in 1926: electron spin in the wave equation (1927-28), the Lamb shift (1947), the proton's finite size (1950s, with the radius puzzle running 2010-2026), CODATA-precision alpha and m_p/m_e, and hadronic and muonic vacuum polarisation.

Evidence that having this data does NOT change the result as the tree uses it:
(a) The result is a theorem about a stated model. It was re-derived exactly here, and no datum enters whether it is true.
(b) Each missing datum corresponds to one of the model's own hypotheses (nonrelativistic and spinless, no QED, clamped nucleus, point nucleus). Each departure was computed: reduced mass 5.4e-4, fine structure 1.3e-5, 1S Lamb shift 2.5e-6, finite size 3.4e-10, hVP ~6e-13. Together they reproduce the real 1H ionization energy to CODATA's quoted digits.
(c) Alpha moved 6.8e-10 between CODATA 2018 and 2022, and D18 holds for every alpha.

Evidence FOR M's hypothesis in this row: the later data show the model is incomplete as a description of real hydrogen, and two residual channels relevant to real atoms are missing or mislabelled on the board (muonic/hadronic VP is unnamed; finite size is filed under the wrong ratio at ledger.py:515-516). Both are ~1e-10 to 1e-12 x eps and change no board conclusion.

For this result, the missing data make the model incomplete as physics, which was always known and named. It is not inaccurate or wrong as a theorem.

SOURCE, READ MYSELF THROUGH alphaXiv:
- Suslov & Trey, arXiv:0707.1887v3, pp.8-10 and p.16:
  - eq (3.2): R_nl, with a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2), n >= 1, 0 <= l <= n-1.
  - eq (3.5): E_n = -m Z^2 e^4/(2 hbar^2 n^2), stated to be independent of l because of the SO(4) symmetry.
  - eqs (3.13)-(3.14): the Pasternack recursion, with <1/r> = Z/(a0 n^2).
  - eq (3.15): <r> = (a0/2Z)(3n^2 - l(l+1)).
  - eqs (4.16)-(4.17): the Sommerfeld-Dirac level and its expansion. The O(mu^2) term coincides with eq (3.5), and the O(mu^4) fine-structure term is the Pauli correction.
- CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787:
  - eq (26): E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1+F), with F set by QED, recoil and other corrections.
  - eqs (28)-(30): the Dirac level for an "infinitely heavy point nucleus", then reduced mass.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: re-run script_path from a copy, check that its encoding is the published theorem and not a toy, and run a vacuity guard with the hypotheses negated
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/h.py and re-ran it. It passed 33/33 with exit 0 (output in verify/rederive/h.out), which reproduces the audit's claimed outcome.

ENCODING. Section 1 is the theorem itself, not a toy. It takes the published normalised R_nl (Suslov-Trey eq 3.2 with a0 = 1/(m alpha) and Z general), substitutes it into the full radial Schrodinger operator with the pure Coulomb potential -Z alpha/r, and gets an exact zero residual for E_n = -m(Z alpha)^2/(2n^2). It also gets exact normalisation and exact <r> = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m Z alpha) for all 21 states with n <= 6. At Z = 1 this is identical to excite.py:954-958, which I read directly.

Two weaknesses, neither of which touches the grade:
(a) Section 5, the dilation, is a tautology as written. It hardcodes E1 = (1+eps)*alpha^2/(2n^2) and then checks E1 == E0*(1+eps), so it cannot fail and never touches the derived result or the tree's function. I re-wired it to excite.hydrogen_levels by a read-only import. It passes there, and it FAILS for a reduced-mass (finite nucleus) model and for an m-independent additive term. So the dilation claim holds, and the re-wired check can tell a true claim from a false one.
(b) The data check in section 6 compares against E_I = 1.096787e7, which is truncated. The actual residual there is 6.48e-7, inside the 9.2e-7 tolerance, so the margin is set by truncation. I recomputed with more digits: the residual is 9.8e-9 with 1.0967877e7 and -6.1e-9 with 1.09678771743e7. Those extra digits are from memory, not READ, but they show that the tolerance was not tuned to force a pass. This is a data cross-check and plays no part in the theorem.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/vac.py, 26/26 behave as expected, output in vac.out):
- Negating the pure-Coulomb hypothesis with -Z alpha/r + beta/r^2, or with a screened -Z alpha e^{-r/b}/r, makes the eigen-equation fail at (1,0), (2,0), (2,1) and (3,2). The true Coulomb potential passes.
- A wrong l in the centrifugal term fails.
- A non-integer n (bound-state hypothesis negated) fails.
- Dropping the normalisation factor fails the norm check.
- Two wrong <r> targets fail: the sign-flipped (3n^2 + l(l+1)), and the Bohr-orbit n^2/(m Z alpha).
- A wrong Dirac alpha^4 coefficient fails.
- Clamped hypothesis negated: with reduced mass the dilation fails.

FINITE CHECK EXTENDED TO GENERAL n. The audit's box limit was n <= 6. I made the eigen-equation symbolic in n and l: with R = e^{-rho/2} rho^l L(rho) and E = -m(Z alpha)^2/(2n^2), the radial equation reduces identically to the associated Laguerre ODE rho L'' + (2l+2-rho)L' + (n-l-1)L = 0. The control E with (n+1)^2 does not reduce. So the level formula holds for all n, given the standard Laguerre ODE. The Kramers-Pasternack <r> check is already symbolic in n and l. That closes the audit's stated WRONG pathway ('if the eigen-equation failed for some n > 6').

Nothing in the re-run contradicts the audit's grade, its hypothesis-drift notes, or its 'what would change the grade' clauses. STANDS is supported. The only things to record are the tautological wiring of section 5 and the truncation-dominated margin of section 6. Both are weaknesses in the audit's check, not discrepancies in the source or the tree.

audits.published_statement: 2208.09014 abstract: 'Brane observers executing appropriate motion through a partially compactified Lorentz invariant bulk spacetime, such as M4 x S1, can send signals along the brane that are instantaneous or even travel backward in time. Nevertheless, causality in the braneworld remains intact.' p.4: 'A quick argument suggests that this cannot happen. In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones.' Sec. 4, eqs. (27)-(28): T = D(1/v - 1/w) = 2D/v_eff, v_eff = gamma(1+Gamma^2 B^2 beta^2); 'always positive ... 0 < T <= 2D/gamma. An instantaneous round trip is possible but closed time-like curves are not.' Eqs. (29)-(32): after adding a circle L' along the brane, the return time is Gamma L'/gamma (1+B/gamma)/(1+Gamma^2B^2beta^2) > 0. Sec. 6: 'all roundtrip signals return to their starting location after a non-negative amount of elapsed time, obviating the possibility of causality-challenging closed timelike curves.' Sec. 5 treats microcausality for a free scalar only; for interactions the paper says 'we expect causality to be robust' and does not show it.
published_hypotheses: The bulk is flat ('Lorentz invariant bulk'): M5 with z ~ z + 2 pi R n, and the identification is purely spatial in a preferred frame (2206.13590 eq. 1; 2208.09014 eq. 1).
In the brane frame the identification is (t', z') ~ (t', z') + (-gamma beta 2 pi R, gamma 2 pi R) (eq. 6/8). A boost B along the brane gives eq. (10).
There is one brane (plus its covering-space images) moving at constant |beta| < 1. It is flat and untilted, and the paper assumes without saying so that it does not back-react on the bulk.
Brane observers move at constant velocity B in (0,1), including supercritical B with Gamma^2 B > 1/(gamma beta^2).

The round trips actually computed are collinear out-and-back trips along x'' built from the envelope velocities v, w (eqs. 20, 25), plus one trip around the added brane circle (eq. 29). The general bulk statement appears only as the p.4 heuristic ('suggests').
Microcausality is shown for a free massless scalar only.

audits.lacked_data: This result is a kinematic theorem about a flat quotient, and its conclusion depends on no measured quantity. beta and R are free parameters. The only fact it uses is |xi|^2 = (2 pi R)^2 > 0, which holds for every beta (sympy check A). GW170817 limits how large beta can be, not this sign. So M's hypothesis that the authors lacked certain data does not bear on this result. The evidence: every check above either has no parameters or holds for all |beta|,|B| < 1, and the 2023-2026 follow-ups (2210.11497, 2602.13448) get the same positive round-trip times over wider classes of motion. What could change the conclusion is a change of hypothesis, not a datum: a curved or back-reacting bulk (Polychronakos sec. 6 finds CTCs around a spinning string, outside H1), a non-translation identification such as a Klein bottle (outside H2), or interacting fields in the microcausality statement (GKLP sec. 5 only says causality is expected). These are the owner's named H1-H3, and they are the part of O3 the tree already keeps OPEN (latticectc.py:95-96). Whether our bulk is flat has not been measured. That is an OPEN physical question, not a defect of the theorem.
audits.grade_evidence: The statement as used (latticectc.py:34-38, :120, :129-131): in a flat bulk, the rank-1 lattice Z xi with xi spacelike has no closed causal curve, whatever the chain length, the boost or the branes present. Re-derivation: m^2|xi|^2 > 0 (z3). K-leg chains are impossible (z3 for K = 1, 2 at each m; every K by the Lagrange identity plus the scalar lemma). GKLP's eqs. 8/10/17/20/22/25/28/32 check out in sympy. v and w are reproduced from the bulk quotient without using GKLP's envelope picture. T > 0 for every integer-winding round trip, including supercritical B. The published GKLP result is narrower than the tree's statement: one brane, collinear round trips, and a heuristic bulk argument on p.4. But the tree presents the wider form as its own theorem, proves it, and names hypotheses H1-H3, which the source satisfies. No moved datum enters. Two discrepancies are recorded; neither changes the mathematics: (i) 'stronger than GKLP, who keep it on branes' (latticectc.py:23) overstates the gap against GKLP's p.4 argument; (ii) 'the two GKLP papers' treats GKLM 2206.13590 as GKLP, and latticectc.py cites no arXiv id.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade becomes NARROWED if any owner uses D21, or 'GKLP's no is forced', outside H1-H3: a warped or back-reacting bulk, a brane with tension, an orientation-reversing compactification, or microcausality with interacting fields. The grade becomes WRONG only if someone exhibits a closed causal curve in a flat translation quotient with a spacelike generator, which the z3 unsat results rule out.

audits.name: FFR 1204.3570 Sec. I: A_tau meant as the self-adjoint (Friedrichs) extension; essential self-adjointness 'not fully resolved'

source.located: arXiv:1204.3570v1 [quant-ph], 16 Apr 2012: C.J. Fewster, L.H. Ford, T.A. Roman, 'Probability distributions for quantum stress tensors in four dimensions', Phys. Rev. D 85, 125038 (2012). Sec. I, p. 2 (the paragraph beginning 'An important point arises here'), with footnote [39] on p. 25, ref. [17] (Reed-Simon II Thm X.23) and ref. [18] (Sanders arXiv:1010.3978).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries(paper='1204.3570') returned page text for pp. 1-3, 10, 12, 15, 20-21 and 25, including the whole Sec. I paragraph and footnote [39]. Ref. [18] (Sanders 1010.3978v3) was also READ at source (pp. 1-2, 5, 9-15). Reed-Simon II Thm X.23 is a textbook theorem with no arXiv copy, so it is NAMED-NOT-READ; the re-derivation exercises its content on a model.

audits.published_statement: FFR 1204.3570 p. 2, verbatim: 'Throughout this paper, all quadratic operators are understood to be normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state. However, the smeared normal ordered operators are defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain in the Hilbert space (assuming a real-valued smearing function) and it is possible that there is more than one way of extending them to provide self-adjoint operators [39]. The operators of greatest interest to us are bounded from below on account of quantum inequalities (see Sect. II A) and so there is a distinguished Friedrichs extension (see Ref. [17], Theorem X.23), whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind when we discuss the probability distribution of individual measurements of the smeared operator in the vacuum state. The question of whether there is more than one self-adjoint extension, i.e., whether the normal ordered expressions fail to be essentially self-adjoint, is nontrivial and not fully resolved. Recent results (not, however, immediately applicable to our situation) and references may be found in Ref. [18]. If there are distinct self-adjoint extensions, their corresponding probability distributions will all share the same moments in the vacuum state.' Footnote [39]: 'The existence of at least one self-adjoint extension is guaranteed on general grounds because the operators commute with complex conjugation of the n-particle wavefunctions in Fock space.' The entry has three parts: a DEFINITION (which self-adjoint realisation is meant), a THEOREM it rests on (Friedrichs), and a STATUS REPORT (essential self-adjointness was open in 2012).
published_hypotheses: P1: quadratic operators are normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum, in 4D Minkowski spacetime. The fields studied are the massless scalar (phi^2, phi-dot^2, rho_S) and electromagnetism (E^2, rho_EM).

P2: the smearing function is real-valued, so the smeared operator is symmetric. The paper's own computations use Lorentzian time-averaging along the time axis at a fixed spatial point, but the Sec. I remark is stated for smeared normal-ordered operators in general.

P3: the operator is defined in the first instance only as a symmetric operator on 'a dense domain'. Sec. I does not specify the domain; p. 10 works with 'states obtained from the vacuum by applying polynomials of smeared fields'.
P4: the operator is bounded from below 'on account of quantum inequalities' (Sect. II A, Eq. (1)). This semiboundedness is the input to the Friedrichs construction.
P5: the Friedrichs extension (Reed-Simon II Thm X.23) is CHOSEN ('It is this operator that we have in mind'). Its lower bound equals the sharpest QI bound.
P6: essential self-adjointness is 'nontrivial and not fully resolved', and Sanders 1010.3978 is 'not, however, immediately applicable'.

P7: if distinct self-adjoint extensions exist, they share the same vacuum moments. The distributions themselves may still differ, because the moment problem may be indeterminate (discussed in Secs. I, IV and VIII A).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (the domain is fixed): noise.py:157-158 realises A_tau as the Friedrichs extension 'on Hadamard vectors', while FFR p. 2 say only 'a dense domain'. The Friedrichs extension depends on the initial domain, so the tree has fixed something FFR leave open. The lower bound C1 uses survives any choice: the Friedrichs lower bound is the infimum of <psi,A psi>/||psi||^2 over the chosen domain, so it is >= -C/tau^4 on any dense linear domain where Fewster 1208.5399 bound (3) holds for every vector. What the tree leaves unstated is that the 'Hadamard vectors' form a dense linear subspace on which A_tau is symmetric. Sanders uses the Wightman domain D_omega, which consists of such vectors. This is a gap in naming, not an error.

WIDENED (field and sampler class), and harmless for this entry: noise.py:154 (H1) takes m >= 0, and noise.py:163-165 (H4) takes a compactly supported sampler root g in W^{2,2}. FFR compute with massless fields and a Lorentzian. The Sec. I remark is functional analysis that holds for any semibounded symmetric operator, and semiboundedness for the tree's class comes from Fewster 1208.5399 (H4), not from FFR. So the widening is not a drift in what FFR Sec. I supports.

ADDED (the tree's own claim, not in FFR): noise.py:160-162, ledger.py:589-590 and specthm.py:2239 say 'a different self-adjoint extension of a semibounded operator need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound'. FFR do not say this, but it is a correct general fact: the Friedrichs extension is the largest semibounded extension in form order, and other extensions can sit strictly below it. data_at_publication.quantity: Status of essential self-adjointness for the operator the tree calls A_tau: the 4D free-scalar energy density, a normal-ordered quadratic operator smeared along a timelike worldline
data_at_publication.value_then: 2012: 'nontrivial and not fully resolved' (FFR p. 2), and Sanders 1010.3978 is 'not immediately applicable'.
data_at_publication.value_now: Sanders 1010.3978v3 (Apr 2012, READ) proves essential self-adjointness on the Wightman domain for the Wick square WITHOUT derivatives, smeared with a SPACETIME test function in class S (finite sums of squares of real test functions), in any quasi-free Hadamard state, on any globally hyperbolic spacetime, for d >= 2 (Thm 5.8). WITH derivatives the result holds only if the one-particle compression is essentially self-adjoint (Thm 5.4). He also gives a distinguished self-adjoint extension as a monotone limit (Thm 5.3). None of these covers a derivative Wick square smeared along a worldline (delta in space), which is the tree's A_tau. Schiappacasse-Fewster-Ford 1711.09477 and Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (both READ) do not settle it either. The first diagonalises a finite-mode truncation in a sphere. The second is 2D CFT, where T(f) is self-adjoint, and its Sec. 5 says its methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'. One discover_papers search found no later resolution; not finding a paper does not prove there is none.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. H3 is ASSUMED either way. A future proof of essential self-adjointness for A_tau would DISCHARGE H3, because Friedrichs would then be the only self-adjoint extension. A proof of the opposite would leave H3 a choice, which is how the tree already carries it. No numerical datum enters this entry.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS: 9 checks, exit 0. The QFT operator is not finite, so both functional-analytic claims were tested on the closed-form model A = -d^2/dx^2 on C_c^inf(0,oo). C1: the form bound is 0 (sympy). C2: the Rayleigh quotient of dilated vectors is 1/(19 s^2) -> 0+, so the Friedrichs (Dirichlet) lower bound equals the form bound and is not attained. C3: the Robin boundary form vanishes, so Robin is a symmetric extension of A. C4: the Robin eigenvector sqrt(2)e^{-x} has eigenvalue -1, below the Friedrichs bound 0; this CONFIRMS the tree's 'a different self-adjoint extension ... need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound'. C5: for phi = x^10 e^{-x}, moments m_0..m_4 computed from the Dirichlet (sine) resolution and from the Robin resolution (atom plus continuum) both agree with <phi, A^n phi> to 30 digits. Yet the Robin measure puts mass 6.279e6 (out of ||phi||^2 = 1.160e12) at -1, below the Friedrichs bound. This CONFIRMS FFR's P7 (shared moments) and shows the shared moments do NOT fix the support, which is why H3 is load-bearing. Not checked: whether the QFT A_tau is essentially self-adjoint (open at source and in the later papers read), and Reed-Simon Thm X.23 itself (NAMED-NOT-READ; exercised on the model only).

later_literature.ref: K. Sanders, arXiv:1010.3978v3 (J. Math. Phys. 53, 042502 (2012)), FFR's ref. [18]
later_literature.what: Proves essential self-adjointness of :phi^2:(f) on the Wightman domain for f in class S (sums of squares of real SPACETIME test functions), in every quasi-free Hadamard representation (Thm 5.8). For Wick squares with derivatives (stress-tensor components) it proves this only when the one-particle compression is essentially self-adjoint (Thm 5.4). It gives a distinguished self-adjoint extension as a monotone strong-resolvent limit (Thm 5.3), and notes that for f in S the Wick square is semibounded, so a Friedrichs extension exists (p. 10). This narrows FFR's open question to derivative Wick squares and to smearings outside S or along a worldline. The tree's A_tau is still in the open part.

later_literature.ref: E.D. Schiappacasse, C.J. Fewster, L.H. Ford, arXiv:1711.09477 (Phys. Rev. D 97, 025013 (2018))
later_literature.what: Bogoliubov-diagonalises a finite-mode truncation of the time-averaged :phi-dot^2: in a sphere. There C_shift is the lowest eigenvalue and also the lower bound of the probability distribution (p. 9). For the Lorentzian, C_shift = -0.0593338 against FFR's moment estimate of -0.0236; both lie inside the Fewster-Eveson bound of -27/128 (p. 20). A finite truncation has no extension ambiguity, so it neither tests nor discharges H3.

In 2D unitary positive-energy CFT the smeared stress tensor is self-adjoint on D(L_0), with the intersection of the D(L_0^k) as a common core (pp. 3, 6). The infimum of the vacuum distribution's support equals the optimal QEI 'on general grounds' (p. 3, Eq. (1.5)), checked for new families at Eq. (4.34). This confirms the Friedrichs/QEI-bound identification where essential self-adjointness holds. Sec. 5 says the methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'.

audits.published_statement:
Abstract: 'We construct a model for the nucleation of a wormhole within a Lorentzian spacetime by employing techniques from topological surgery and Morse theory. In our framework, a 0-surgery process describes the neighborhood of the nucleation point inside a compact region of spacetime, yielding a singular Lorentzian cobordism that connects two spacelike regions with different topologies. To avoid the singularity at the critical point of the Morse function, we employ the Misner trick of taking a connected sum with a closed 4-manifold -- namely CP^2 -- to obtain an everywhere nondegenerate Lorentzian metric. This connected sum replaces the naked singularity with a region containing closed timelike curves. The obtained spacetime is nonsingular, but violates all the standard energy conditions.'

Sec. IV.B: the Morse spacetime (13) has type-IV regions under criterion (19) (Fig. 9) and so violates all the standard energy conditions.

Sec. IV.C: there are regions where T w w < 0 (Fig. 12), and a type-IV point p=(1,0,0,0) on CP^2. Eq. (24): 'the numerical factor 2 is arbitrary and can be replaced by any real number zeta > 1 ... changing zeta merely shifts, thins, or expands the regions where the energy conditions are violated; it does not eliminate them altogether.'

Sec. V.D: homotopies H1-H4 built from smooth b(eta), c(eta) and a path alpha(eta) in SO(4). 'Because the entire deformation is smooth and nonsingular, the resulting Lorentzian metric on the neck remains free of singularities, and no further explicit expression is required for our purposes.'

Sec. I: 'The conclusions we present, apart from the investigations of the energy conditions on these spacetimes, are purely kinematic'.
published_hypotheses: P1 Classical and 4-dimensional. A spacetime has an everywhere non-degenerate, TIME-ORIENTABLE Lorentzian metric with signature (-,+,+,+) (Def. 6). The result is kinematic: the metric is built by eq. (2) from a Riemannian metric plus a line field, not solved from field equations.
P2 The Hawking-Borde setting: the transition is confined to a compact timelike tube W with boundary Sigma_i U T U Sigma_f.
P3 kink(dW; g_L) = 1 is ASSUMED. The paper motivates it as the ambient spacetime being asymptotically flat (sec. III.D).
P4 A single 0-surgery (one index-1 Morse critical point, eq. 1), with initial region Sigma_i = D^3 (genus 0, footnote 5).

P5 The Riemannian metric on M is the graph metric (11), and the paper says the choice is 'arbitrary'. CP^2 carries the Fubini-Study metric (23) with a free Lambda > 0. The CP^2 line field (20)/(21) 'is not unique'.
P6 The construction factor in (2) is 2. Eq. (24) says any zeta > 1 is admissible, but the paper's own metrics (22), (35) and (36) use 2.

P7 Gluing uses the Mars-Senovilla rigging formalism with sufficient C^1 matching. The annuli carry free profile functions a(tau), b(tau), alpha(sigma), beta(sigma), constrained by (37), (38) and (40). The neck S^3 x I has a free radius R and free smooth b(eta), c(eta), alpha(eta).

P8 The energy conditions are the standard ones with no cosmological constant. T is the Einstein tensor of the constructed metric; there is no matter model. The evidence is pointwise Hawking-Ellis type plus one WEC plot, with no integrated figure.
P9 W has NO spin structure (u(dW)=0 while kink=1 mod 2); only Spin^c exists.
P10 Explicit scope exclusion: QFT on the compactly generated Cauchy horizon, where the renormalized stress-energy tensor diverges, is 'beyond the scope of the present classical analysis' (sec. I.A).

audits.published_statement: Sec. IV p.10: 'Flat spacetime is a solution of the semi-classical Einstein equations for vanishing expectation value of T_ab and cosmological term, with the quantum matter field in its Lorentz invariant vacuum ground state.' 'The linear response equation (3.4) around a Minkowski background, eta_ab, can be decomposed ...' giving (4.1), whose right side is the retarded non-local term (1/2) Int d^4x' Pi^(ret)cd_ab(x;x') h_cd(x'). (4.2): Kallen-Lehmann spectral representation of the Fourier transform Pi^(i)(ret)(k^0, vec k) = Int dw rho^(i)(w, vec k)/(w - k^0 - i eps), i = T,S. Between (4.3) and (4.4): 'In Fourier space the non-local real convolution in eq.(4.1) becomes a simple multiplication with h_cd(k).' (4.4): three subtractions at k^2 = 0. (4.5a)/(4.5b): the tensor and scalar dispersion formulae in k^2. p.12: 'The possibility of a finite number of non-propagating (global) modes in the scalar sector at k = 0 cannot be excluded by this argument, and must be investigated by imposing appropriate boundary conditions at spatial infinity. We do not treat this possibility in this paper.' Abstract: 'the flat space solution to the semi-classical Einstein equations for n = 4 is stable to all perturbations on distance scales much larger than the Planck length.' Sec. V p.14: '... a completely satisfactory stability of flat space for all local perturbations obeying the inequality (4.6).' Nothing in the paper treats a bounded, shell-bounded, or partially flat region (the words 'shell', 'cavity', 'bounded region', 'finite region', 'Dirichlet', 'Robin' do not occur; checked).
published_hypotheses: S1 background: Minkowski spacetime eta_ab, a solution of (2.9) with <T_ab> = 0 and Lambda = 0 (p.10)

S2 state: the quantum matter field in its Lorentz (Poincare) invariant vacuum ground state (p.10; abstract 'vacuum state of Minkowski spacetime') -- this is what makes Pi^(ret)(x;x') depend on x - x' only and admit the Kallen-Lehmann form (4.2)
S3 the response integral in (4.1) runs over all x' with retarded (causal) support (theta(t - t'), p.9) -- in Fourier space over (k^0, vec k) in R^4, where convolution becomes multiplication (p.10)

S4 large-N free scalar field(s), arbitrary m > 0 and xi; for the tensor positivity step only positivity of rho^(T) is used ('causality, a bounded Hamiltonian, and a well-defined positive Hilbert space norm', p.11) -- generality over MATTER, not over domain
S5 renormalised Lambda, 1/G_N, alpha, beta fixed by subtraction at k^2 = 0 (4.4)
S6 O(1) fourth-order coefficients for the 'Planck-scale only' conclusion (p.12, V p.14)
S7 k = 0 global scalar modes excluded from the analysis; they would need boundary conditions at spatial infinity (p.12)

S2 is a second, independent reason AMM does not transfer to a shell exterior (the state outside a shell is not in general the Minkowski vacuum). Omitting it understates the decline; it does not enlarge any use of AMM.
