There 'local' qualifies the k-space inequality (4.6), not a spatial region. The tree follows the proof's domain, not the gloss.

rederivation.outcome: 36 checks, 0 failed. A (19): the load-bearing sentences are verbatim in AMM's text layer: the Lorentz-invariant vacuum, 'around a Minkowski background', (4.1) as a retarded convolution over x', 'In Fourier space the non-local real convolution in eq.(4.1) becomes a simple multiplication', the labels (4.2), (4.5a), (4.5b), 'boundary conditions at spatial infinity ... We do not treat this possibility', the abstract and V gloss, and the p.11 matter-generality clause. No bounded-region, shell, cavity, Dirichlet or Robin treatment occurs. B (4): the owner's statement is at linstab.py:86-92, the pin at :341, and it is a record() at :1049, not a chk(). C (3, numpy): a translation-invariant retarded kernel on a translation-invariant (periodic) lattice is diagonalised EXACTLY by plane waves (max residual 3e-13, eigenvalue = Fourier symbol). The same kernel on a region bounded at one end (Toeplitz block) leaves a plane-wave residual of 4.14 and its spectrum collapses to kern[0], not the symbol. So AMM's 'convolution -> multiplication' step needs S2+S3 and fails on a bounded region. D (exact, sympy): D1, the full-line wave equation is Fourier-stable, yet on the half-line exterior x > R with a wall condition u_x(R) = -kappa u(R), the L^2 mode e^{kappa(t-(x-R))} grows at rate kappa, so 'stable' is not inherited. D2, the full-line tachyonic equation is Fourier-unstable, yet on an interval of length pi/(2 mu) with Dirichlet walls every mode is stable, so 'unstable' is not inherited on a bounded region. D3 CONTROL, on an unbounded half-line exterior with Dirichlet at R the tachyonic instability SURVIVES, so the decline means 'must be computed afresh', not 'fails'. E: the causal past of every exterior event meets the shell world-tube, so (4.1)'s retarded integral at an exterior point runs over the non-flat region. The toys are illustrations of the logic, not models of the semiclassical device. audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis asked of this result: what did AMM lack, and would having it change the conclusion? The result audited here is a SCOPE fact about AMM's proof (the domain, state and kernel it assumes), not a numerical conclusion. No datum enters it: no measured constant, no fitted value. What AMM lacked for the tree's case is not data but a PROBLEM they did not pose: a flat region bounded by a shell, in the state the shell induces, with the retarded kernel reaching into the shell's world-tube. The paper says as much. It treats the Minkowski vacuum on eta_ab (p.10), leaves global k = 0 modes to 'boundary conditions at spatial infinity' (p.12), and lists curved and horizon backgrounds as future applications (V, pp.13-14). Evidence either way: (i) AMM make no bounded-region claim that could be wrong, so the conclusion is not moved by anything learned since. (ii) The later rigorous work the tree holds (GMMPS 2604.01047) is again posed on all of R^4, so the gap is still unfilled, not filled against AMM. (iii) The toy controls show that the missing computation could come out either way (D1 stable->unstable, D2 unstable->stable, D3 unstable survives). So nothing here is a defect in AMM. It is an absent calculation, and M's 'lacked certain data' does not apply to this item: its conclusion carries no datum that could have moved.
audits.grade_evidence: The published statement and hypotheses support the tree's use. AMM's flat-space analysis is posed around a Minkowski background eta_ab with the matter field in its Lorentz-invariant vacuum (p.10). Its (4.1) response is a retarded convolution over x', which 'In Fourier space ... becomes a simple multiplication' (p.10), and (4.2)-(4.5b) are Fourier-space formulae in (k^0, vec k) and k^2. No bounded or shell-bounded region is treated anywhere, and the global k = 0 modes are left to boundary conditions at spatial infinity (p.12). All of this is asserted verbatim by the script. The re-derivation agrees: plane waves diagonalise a translation-invariant kernel exactly on a translation-invariant domain and fail on a region bounded at one end (residual 3e-13 vs 4.14). Exact toy models show that both 'stable' and 'unstable' can fail to be inherited when a wall is added. The tree uses the result only NEGATIVELY: FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_AMM = False, a record pin, not a check that can fail. The hypotheses it omits (Poincare vacuum, retarded past support, global-mode boundary condition) are further reasons for the same decline, so none narrows it. No datum is involved, so none can have moved. Recorded, not repaired: (a) the citation '(IV, (4.2)-(4.5))' leaves out (4.1) and the unnumbered Fourier sentence, which is a completeness note, not an error. (b) 'neither stable nor unstable transfers' holds only as 'not inherited from the proof'. Control D3 shows an instability can survive on an unbounded exterior, so the line must not be quoted as 'the flat exterior is known to be unstable' or 'known not to be stable'.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED or WRONG would need a published result that establishes AMM's (or GMMPS's) verdict for a flat region bounded by a shell, or more generally for a locally flat region in a non-Minkowski state. Examples: a local or microlocal stability theorem for semiclassical gravity whose hypotheses a shell exterior meets, or a proof that AMM's Fourier-space dispersion relation governs perturbations supported away from the shell up to controlled errors. Such a result would make 'does not inherit' stale for that class. The later-literature search that could find one was refused here (alphaXiv quota), so a completed discover_papers run over 'local stability semiclassical gravity / bounded region / Hadamard state perturbation' is the open item. A fresh page-image read of AMM pp.10-14 contradicting the text layer's sentences would also reopen it. No datum can change it.

verifiers.reason:
The auditor could not read the paper fresh because alphaXiv refused the requests (quota). In this stage alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/0209075v1 succeeded and returned pp.1, 4, 5 and 10-14. Every load-bearing sentence matches the source verbatim:
- p.10 "Lorentz invariant vacuum ground state" and "around a Minkowski background".
- (4.1) is the retarded convolution over d^4x'.
- (4.2) is "given for the Fourier transform" Pi(k^0, vec k).
- p.10, the unnumbered sentence: "In Fourier space the non-local real convolution in eq.(4.1) becomes a simple multiplication with h_cd(k)".
- (4.4)-(4.5b) are written in k^2.
- p.12: "boundary conditions at spatial infinity. We do not treat this possibility in this paper."
- The abstract and the V p.14 gloss ("all local perturbations obeying the inequality (4.6)") also match.

I also searched the de-spaced text layer for boundary vocabulary. It turns up only causal/retarded boundary conditions, surface terms, spatial infinity, and one citation in the introduction (ref. [27], a 1+1-D moving boundary in other authors' work). None of these is a bounded-region treatment by AMM, so the auditor's word-list claim holds.

The strongest attack I tried: does V's "all local perturbations" plus finite propagation speed carry the verdict over to perturbations supported in the exterior? It does not, for three reasons:
- "local" qualifies the k-space inequality (4.6), not a spatial region.
- AMM's criterion (p.10) is unbounded growth in time. That is an asymptotic, global property, which a domain-of-dependence argument cannot deliver.
- The kernel is evaluated in the state, and the state outside a shell is not the Poincare vacuum (S2).

The tree uses the result only negatively: FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_AMM = False is a record pin, not a check that can fail. The hypotheses the tree omits (S2, S3, S7) only strengthen that decline. No datum is involved, so "lacked data" does not apply.

One small imprecision, recorded and not grade-moving. Check E says (4.1)'s retarded integral "runs over the non-flat region", but that integrand is weighted by h(x'). The decisive reason the result does not transfer is S2+S3, which check C shows: the kernel is not translation-invariant once the region is bounded.

Later literature: discover_papers ran this time and returned 2512.00503, 2506.17149, 2605.24103, 2608.31008 and 2507.05237. Judged by title and abstract only (none was read in full), none transfers AMM's verdict to a bounded or shell-exterior region. The literature gap therefore stays an OPEN sub-item, as the audit records, and it cannot move the grade of a non-inheritance use.

ENCODING. Section A is the real evidence: verbatim reads against the source text layer. Sections C, D and E test toys of the logic, not the theorem. The audit says so itself, and the grade does not rest on them.

Independent source check. The text layer drops 'fi' ligatures ('spatialinnity'), so an absence test for 'finiteregion' could pass vacuously. I re-grepped for 'niteregion' and 'nitevolume'. Both are absent, so the absence claim survives the ligature loss. The words 'region', 'bounded' and 'boundary' do occur, but only for 'unbounded in time', 'causal boundary conditions', boundary/surface terms, and a cited moving-boundary paper [27]. A 'Casimir vacuum' appears in Sec. I, but it is the setting of cited fluctuation computations, not AMM's stability analysis. None of these is a bounded-region stability treatment. The scope point is also stronger than the audit cites: Appendix (A20) writes the transform explicitly as Int d^n x e^{ik(x-x')} <T_ab(x) T_cd(x')>. That is a Fourier transform over all of R^n of a function of x - x' only, which directly supports 'Fourier-transforms over all of Minkowski space' and S2.

VACUITY GUARDS (my script verify/rederive/gr-qc_0209075_flat-exterior-scope_vacuity.py, 6/6):
- V1: with S2 negated (an x-dependent kernel on a periodic domain), plane waves fail (residual 4.31). This confirms S2 as an independent reason for the decline.
- V2 caveat on toy C: with the audit's compact 6-site kernel, the plane-wave failure sits entirely in a boundary layer one kernel-width deep (bulk residual 5e-15, edge 2.21). The 'spectrum collapses to kern[0]' result is a finite-section artefact of a non-normal triangular Toeplitz matrix. On its own, toy C does not show that the Fourier analysis fails far from the wall.
- V2b: with a long-range power-law kernel the defect reaches mid-bulk (2.4e-3 at site 32). So the decline away from the shell rests on the retarded kernel's long range plus S2, not on toy C alone.
- V3: D1's growing mode needs the 'wrong-sign' Robin condition. With the opposite sign there is no positive root and no L2 growing mode, so D1 is not vacuous, but it is a named-hypothesis toy.
- V4: check E as encoded is a tautology. It tests (r-R_s+eps)-(r-R_s)==eps and would pass the same algebra with a spacelike separation.
- V4b: the geometric claim behind E is true, but only for a shell that has existed for all past time. With a shell formed at t0 > t-(r-R_s), the past cone does not reach it. 'Every exterior event' therefore carries a NAMED hypothesis (an eternal/static shell). This narrows only one of the audit's three supplementary reasons, not the tree's use.

None of this touches what the tree uses. The tree uses one READ scope fact, negatively and as a non-failing record pin, and that fact is confirmed verbatim at source plus (A20). No datum is involved.

(a) check E is vacuous as written;
(b) toy C's bounded-region failure is boundary-local for compact kernels;
(c) E needs an eternal shell;

- The Planck length is a scale that bounds the validity criterion, not a fitted number.
- The p.14 remark that the predictions are "not in complete disagreement with observations" (line 2384) is a qualitative gloss on the stability conclusion, not an input to the domain of the proof.

- Mbar shift with exact hbar: +3.064e-10.

So each moves_conclusion 'No' follows.

Both G reanalyses were READ AT SOURCE here through alphaXiv; the audit had them only from a sibling stage. 1905.09551 Table 4 (p.31) and p.14: the data are 16 inputs, and MTE with kappa = 3.9 reproduces 6.67429(15). That confirms 'expansion factor 3.9 over 16 inputs that disagree' (Q = 198 on 15 degrees of freedom, p.10). 2209.07416 (p.1, p.7): it uses CODATA 2018's 16 results and recommends G = 6.6740 +-0.0015 at 90%.

Three discrepancies in the data claim were found. They are recorded, not repaired, and none moves the grade.

(1) The value_now row and later_literature both say 'reanalyses give 6.67390-6.67408 with u up to 0.00030'. That understates 1905.09551 Table 4. Across its non-multiplicative methods the consensus values run from 6.67377 (LOP) through 6.67380 (MP) and 6.67389 (REML/BG/MM) to 6.67408 (LAP/BMM). The uncertainties reach 0.00060 (MP) and 0.00117 (LOP), and the LOP 95% interval runs 6.67127-6.67577. Computed, the widest of these is still inside the +-1e-3 envelope: the LOP lower bound is -4.54e-4 relative, which moves m by 2.27e-4. So the conclusion survives, but the quoted range is a subset of what the source prints.

(2) 'Arguing CODATA underestimates u(G) by up to about 10x' is not a statement of 2209.07416. The paper says only 'heavily underestimating'. The 10x figure compares its 90% half-width (0.0015) with CODATA's 1-sigma (0.00015). Like for like, its 68% interval (+0.0007/-0.0009) is 4.7-6x CODATA's u. audits.lacked_data: This tests M's hypothesis for this result: did the earlier editions lack data, and did it matter? (a) PDG 2024 and 2025 did not have CODATA 2022. Their m_e, m_p and m_n sat 4.60, 4.38 and 2.63 sigma (of the 2018 errors) away from today's values. Here M's premise is literally true: the earlier values were wrong at their own stated precision. But the move is 1.4e-9 relative and the same fraction for each mass (m_e/m_p = 5.4461702149e-4 in both editions), so nothing the tree concludes changes; this was computed. (b) PDG 2024 and 2025 did not include CMS 2024 on m_W, and the value went from 80369 to 80362 MeV. Computed: alpha_W changes by 0.02% and the log10 suppression by 0.03 decade. (c) The W mass is still CONTESTED because of CDF 2022. Taking CDF's value changes the instanton suppression by 0.29 of about 161 decades and E_sph by 0.09%. No refusal or price the tree states reads m_W at that precision. (d) m_s moved from 93.5 to 92.9 MeV and m_b from 4183 to 4186 MeV; both are only printed as Yukawas. (e) The tree's capture is already the newest edition (2026), so for the values nothing available is missing. The one place where missing data could change the reading is N_F. A table of observed states cannot say that no heavier SU(2)-doublet generation exists. That is H-3GEN, which the tree does not name; evidence for it exists in the literature but was not read here. Evidence both ways: data did move, which confirms M's premise in form, and it moved nothing the tree concludes, which refutes the premise for this result's conclusions.
audits.grade_evidence: Every numerical datum STANDS. The capture reproduces PDG 2026's own data file to 9 significant figures: the md5 matches, an independent parse agrees, and the largest rounding gap is 1.94 sigma (e). The e, p and n values equal CODATA 2022. Every derived tree figure re-derives: m_N, m_e/m_p, y_t 0.9914, y_e 2.935e-6, lightest baryon p, and the count of 3. No moved datum changes a conclusion, computed for each: CODATA 2018 to 2022 (1.4e-9 relative, ratios unchanged), m_W from 80369 to 80362, the contested CDF 80433.5 (0.29 of about 161 decades; 0.09% of E_sph), and m_t, m_s and m_b. H-TREE names the quark-mass scheme and 't direct' (massform.py:751-754). The narrowing comes from one hypothesis the tree leaves out. massform.py:1041-1048 reads the count of OBSERVED charged leptons as the number of generations N_F. The anomaly vertex, ceil(B/N_F), E_sph/(N_F m_p) and the extra-lepton count all use it (:2055, :2127, :2141, :2155). The tree names only PDG's status filter, not H-3GEN, the hypothesis that no further SU(2)-doublet generation exists. This is a limitation that needs naming, not an error: the count is right, and the hypothesis is well supported empirically in literature not read here. The grade is not WRONG, because there is no counterexample. It is not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no moved or contested datum changes a conclusion. Discrepancies are recorded and nothing is repaired: the electron mass marked '(READ)' is the capture's 9-s.f. rendering, 1.94 sigma from PDG's printed value.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: It becomes STANDS if the tree names H-3GEN at n_generations() (massform.py:1041) as a hypothesis N_F's use rests on, or cites a READ source for it. It becomes DATA-DEPENDENT if a tree conclusion turns out to read m_W, m_e or m_p at the 1e-3 level or finer (none was found), or if the RPP text, once read, shows the capture's W average is not the one the tree takes it to be. It becomes WRONG only if the capture is shown not to match the PDG file, and it does match: all 14 rows agree at 9 s.f. The RPP text (the W mini-review, the CDF footnote and the quark-mass scheme notes) is still NAMED-NOT-READ. Reading it could add a hypothesis, but it cannot change a value the file already fixes.

The audit holds. I found nothing that refutes it.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/pdg-2026-capture.py and ran it. It exits 0 with 0 failures, and every number the audit quotes reproduces:
- The md5 values of mass_width_2026.txt and particle2026.csv match the capture header.
- All 14 rows match float('%.9g' % PDG2026). The largest rounding gaps are e at 1.94 sigma and p at 1.48 sigma.
- The CODATA 2018 to 2022 moves are 4.60, 4.38 and 2.63 sigma, each about 1.4e-9 relative, and m_e/m_p = 5.4461702149e-4 under both editions.
- m_N = 938.9187555, v = 246.21965 GeV, y_t = 0.991364 and y_e = 2.93503e-6.
- N_F = 3, and tau' and nu(tau') carry status 4 with mass -1.
- With the CDF W mass, the log10 suppression shifts by +0.286 and E_sph by -0.089%.

The tree's own checks also pass. `pdgcapture.py --verify` reports 572 rows agree. `python3.12 massform.py --selftest` reports SELFTEST OK, with every capture fixture [ok].

ENCODING. I compared the script line by line with massform.py:
- n_generations() at :1041-1045 counts family == lepton and Q3 == -3 in the capture. The script uses the same predicate.
- alpha_W = (2 m_W/v)^2/4pi at :2105-2110 and log10 exp(-4pi/alpha_W) at :2113 match the script.
- E_sph = 2 m_W/alpha_W x B_fn at :2134-2137 holds B fixed as READ terms, so the script's E_sph sensitivity with B held fixed matches how the tree uses it.
- The 'independent' parse really is separate: it uses fixed FORTRAN column slices and does not touch pdgcapture.py or the particle loader.

Two limits in the encoding, neither of which changes any conclusion:
(a) The y_t check and the W-sensitivity block use hardcoded 172.6 and 80.362, not values read from the capture. When I mutated the capture's top mass to 162500 MeV, the y_t check still passed. The capture-vs-PDG row check failed at 37 sigma, so the combined chain still holds.
(b) The 'PDG2026 = CODATA 2022 to 1e-9 relative' tolerance tells the editions apart with little room. The edition gap is 1.35e-9 to 1.5e-9 relative against a 1e-9 tolerance, so it works, but the margin is only about 35%.

VACUITY GUARD. I fed the script six mutated copies of the capture:
- M0, identical copy: 0 failures.
- M1, e changed in its last digit to 0.51099895: FAIL at 4.31 sigma.
- M3, W set to CDF's 80433.5: FAIL at 8.94 sigma.
- M4, top set to the MS-bar value 162.5 GeV: FAIL at 37.4 sigma.
- M5, proton rows removed: crashes with KeyError, so it does not pass.
- M2, a status-4 tau'- row (lepton, Q3 = -3) added: the N_F check FAILS with 4 charged leptons.

The script is therefore not vacuous. M2 also shows something about the tree itself, because the script mirrors n_generations() exactly. N_F = 3 comes only from the capture's status-4 exclusion; the capture header reads 'excluded: ... PDG status 4 NotInPDT (fourth generation and diquarks)'. The tree uses that count as Rubakov-Shaposhnikov's 'number of generations' at :2055, :2127, :2141 and :2155. The selection rule counts every SU(2) doublet generation, whether or not it has been observed.

I grepped massform.py for fourth / generation / LEP / N_nu. Every hit is either the RS quote or lattice N_f = 2+1+1. The hypothesis list H-TREE through H-THERM at :751-840 has no hypothesis on the number of generations. H-3GEN is therefore unnamed in the tree, as the audit says.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported:
- Not STANDS, because the hypothesis is missing.
- Not WRONG, because the count is right and nothing contradicts it.
- Not DATA-DEPENDENT, because no data that moved or is disputed changes a conclusion; each case was computed.

The audit's sources marked NAMED-NOT-READ (the RPP text, CDF, CMS, the fourth-generation exclusions) could not be checked here, and the audit labels them correctly. Its grade does not rest on any of them.

audits.published_statement: Fewster 1208.5399 p.44 sec.5.1: 'the classical minimally coupled scalar field obeys the WEC by virtue of a decomposition of the energy density as a sum of squares. This is not true for the nonminimally coupled field, and indeed the energy density can be made arbitrarily negative at any given point.' Barcelo-Visser gr-qc/0003025 eq.(2.5): WEC = [(1-2xi)(phi')^2 + 1/2 (grad phi)^2 + V(phi) - xi((phi^2)'' + 2 grad(phi grad phi))]/(kappa - xi phi^2) >= 0; then 'In the minimally coupled case (xi = 0) it is generically satisfied. Only a large negative potential, for example, a negative cosmological constant, could provide a violation of WEC.' Buttazzo 1307.3536 sec.2: 'we write the classical Higgs potential as V_0 = -m_0^2/2 |H_0|^2 + lambda_0 |H_0|^4'. With |H|^2 = phi^2/2 this is the tree's V(phi) = -(mu^2/2)phi^2 + (lambda/4)phi^4, mu^2 = lambda v^2.
published_hypotheses: A classical (c-number) field: Fewster's 'classical', which he contrasts with the quantum field.
Minimal coupling, xi = 0 (Fewster; Barcelo-Visser 'minimally coupled case (xi = 0)').
A potential that is not large and negative (Barcelo-Visser). Measured from the vacuum this means V - V(v) >= 0, which the Mexican hat with lambda > 0 satisfies.
A normal (non-phantom) sign for the kinetic term: L = -(1/2)(grad phi)^2 - V.
A tree-level (classical) Higgs potential with lambda > 0 (Buttazzo sec.2). Beyond tree level lambda_eff turns negative at large field (Buttazzo sec.4.2), and the tree carries that separately.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED, UNNAMED: minimal coupling (xi = 0). The theorem at massform.py:393-411 and its code at massform.py:1917-1964 (t00_decomposes asks higgs.T_scalar, 'L = -(s/2)(grad phi)^2 - V', higgs.py:328-341) is for xi = 0, but section 6 (massform.py:752-770) names only H-TREE-V and H-REAL. The board's own higgs.py:110-135 says the Higgs is 'THE ONE FIELD THAT MUST HAVE' xi. Computed here (C5a): in FLAT space the Hilbert T_00 gains -xi Lap(phi^2). A static witness at xi = 1/6 (C5b) has T_00 - V(v) = -0.020975 < 0 at a point, where the xi = 0 value there is +0.009025. So the POINTWISE sentence 'energy above the vacuum is >= 0, and zero only where phi_t = 0, grad phi = 0 and |phi| = v' needs xi = 0. The added term is a spatial divergence, and its period integral equals the xi = 0 integral exactly (C5d). So the INTEGRATED statement that D29 uses ('any change of phi about v costs energy') survives any xi in flat space. In curved space the xi R phi^2 term enters directly, and the WEC can fail (Barcelo-Visser eq. 2.5).

WEAKENED, IMPLICIT: the classical-field hypothesis. The tree writes 'THEOREM, on the tree-level potential (H-TREE-V)' (massform.py:408-409), and 'tree-level' carries 'classical' only by implication. It is never named for T_00. Fewster pp.44-45 (READ): quantum fields sustain negative local energy density, e.g. 'long-lasting negative energy densities can be sustained by quantum fields as shown by the example of the Casimir effect'. The pointwise positivity therefore does not survive quantisation. The global statement (energy above a true ground state is >= 0) needs the vacuum to be the ground state, which is the metastable case the tree already carries at massform.py:414-420.
IMPLICIT, NOT NAMED: flat spacetime, the Minkowski ETA in higgs.T_scalar. It is harmless when xi = 0, and it is where the xi drift bites when xi != 0.
IMPLICIT, SATISFIED: lambda > 0, i.e. m_H^2 > 0 (higgs.py:267-270, lambda = m_H^2/(2v^2)). The vacuity guard C4b shows lambda < 0 breaks the bound.

PRECISION, NOT A FAULT (H-REAL, massform.py:410-412, 761-763): for the doublet, 'ANY change of phi about v COSTS energy' should read 'costs non-negative energy'. Motion along the vacuum orbit Phi^+Phi = v^2/2 and pure-gauge changes cost zero. For the radial mode eps the sentence is exact, zero only at eps = 0 or 2 (C2c).

H-REAL is carried by the tree as 'claimed, NOT computed and NOT read' (massform.py:410-412, 761-763; D29 at massform.py:2889-2905). It is COMPUTED here (C3a, C3b), not repaired in the tree. For SU(2)xU(1) with a doublet, the gauge-invariant Hilbert T_00 = (1/2) sum_a (|E^a|^2 + |B^a|^2) + sum_mu |D_mu Phi|^2 + V, and V - V_min = lambda(Phi^+Phi - v^2/2)^2 >= 0 for lambda > 0 (z3 unsat). The check holds on the same classical, xi = 0, flat, non-ghost hypotheses. It says nothing about a gauge-fixed canonical tensor with Faddeev-Popov ghosts.

verifiers.reason:
The audit graded OPEN for one reason: it could not read the literature (all four alphaXiv calls hit quota, and arXiv is proxy-refused). That reason no longer holds. In this run alphaXiv answered, and I READ the following at source.

(1) Lange et al. arXiv:2010.06620v2, pp.1 and 4 with Table II. mu = m_p/m_e drift is -8(36)e-18/yr, and the coupling (c^2/mu)(dmu/dPhi) is 7(45)e-8. The caption says the limits are "for a linear temporal variation and a coupling to changes of the gravitational potential". The mu value is inferred using external restrictions on alpha and on X_q (Ref. [8]) and computed sensitivity coefficients. The results "support the validity of [LPI] in the solar system in the present epoch". So: ratio-only, finite B, a sampled location, model-dependent.

(2) Uzan arXiv:1009.5514v1.
- p.23 Table 5: every system constrains g_p, mu and alpha_EM only, plus "other hypothesis".
- p.54 Table 10: quasar H2/NH3 bounds at z ~ 0.7-3. One weighted mean is a 3.5 sigma "detection" whose authors "do not claim a detection".
- p.89 names the audit's dropped hypothesis at source: "assuming that the masses of the standard model fermions all vary with v so that the Yukawa couplings are assumed constant". It names the sampled-places hypothesis too: "homogeneous in space (so that it may not be applied as such in the case a chameleon mechanism is at work)".
- p.88 eq. (184) gives Lambda_QCD proportional to (m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27), which supports the 2/9.
- p.99 records a Milky Way NH3 offset of (2.2 +- 0.4 +- 0.3)e-8 that "could be interpreted as a variation".
So the audit's drifts B1, B2 and B3 now attach to READ statements rather than restatements.

(3) Decisive, and not in the audit: discover_papers surfaced a present-epoch, local, nonzero claim, which I then READ at source.
- Vorotyntseva & Levshakov arXiv:2503.17665, pp.1 and 8-9: Delta(m_e/m_p)/(m_e/m_p), Sgr B2(N) minus Orion-KL, is (-3.7 +- 0.5)e-7. That is "non-zero signal at 7.5 sigma", still 5.3 sigma with 50 kHz systematics, and "not explained by known systematic effects". The authors interpret it as dark-matter coupling and say independent measurements are needed.
- Shtein, Vorotyntseva & Levshakov arXiv:2609.03431 (Sep 2026), pp.3, 12-14: the Sgr B2 indication is restated as (-3.4 +- 0.4)e-7 across three papers. Their seven-cloud disk survey (D_GC 1.5-13 kpc) gives (0.5 +- 0.5)e-7, i.e. null. The paper frames the target explicitly as a DM-Higgs-field coupling, which is variation of the vev, the very thing P-UNIFORM denies.

The audit's own criterion for DATA-DEPENDENT is "a READ measurement ... showing a nonzero present-epoch or local variation of mu ... beyond its errors". That criterion is now met literally. Hence DATA-DEPENDENT, not OPEN.

Guarding against over-representation in both directions:
- It is a single group's unconfirmed "indication". The authors themselves ask for verification. The Sgr B2 lines are broad (FWHM ~26 MHz against 7). An earlier Galactic offset from the same lineage was attributed to rest-frequency issues. It is NOT an established variation, so WRONG is not supported.
- Computed in verify/refute/fermion-mass-constancy.py, with all checks passing: on H-YUK-FIXED it maps to dv/v of about -4.6e-7 to -5.3e-7 (H1) or -3.6e-7 to -4.1e-7 (H2), over S = 0.0466-0.0935. That is seven orders below anything bearing on C1's refusal of r < 1. No D27, S10 or SR5 verdict moves, and C5 needs no P-UNIFORM.
- Discounting the Sgr B2 indication entirely, the floor grade is NARROWED. The ratio-only, finite-B, sampled-place, Yukawa-fixed and LPI/linear-drift hypotheses are all READ at source, and the auditor's sympy map is confirmed independently (K_mu = -7(1-S)/9; null direction d(1/alpha_s) = -7/(2 pi) per unit d ln v).

Auditor errors found:
- None in the computation. The rederive script re-ran ALL PASS, exit 0.
- One minor mischaracterisation: the "circularity risk" says clock mu-dot limits assume LPI. Lange's limits are themselves an LPI test, assuming only linear drift and annual Phi coupling. That drift was recorded and not graded, so the grade is unaffected.
- Under the now-READ data, the audit's lacked_data claim that "nothing computed or read here indicates any variation" is superseded.

The cited tree lines check out: massform.py:220-226 ('not read here', 'No owner boolean asserts it'), :815-819 (C1 rests on P-UNIFORM; C5 does not), :1621-1627 (P_UNIFORM_STATUS='PREMISE', VEV_IS_UNIFORM = P_UNIFORM), address.py:99-116 (H1 and H2 named), and C1 on D15/D16 (massform.py:622, 797, 2442).

ENCODING: what the script checks is the inference map from any ratio bound B to the vev, not the measurement itself. That is the right target, given that the tree cites no value. A1/A2 are first-order, tree-level and ignore electromagnetic and running corrections; the hypotheses are named in the docstring.

Two weaknesses:
(a) B1/B2 are TAUTOLOGICAL. Every nonzero 1x7 row has rank 1 and nullity 6 (mutation M3 confirms this on 200 random rows). 'Rank 1' is therefore not a physics finding. The content is B3/B4, which name explicit null directions with dv != 0, and I re-confirmed both for symbolic S. B4's compensator is -7/(2 pi), independent of S.
(b) C1 is hard-coded arithmetic. D3 is checked at a single point; I confirmed it holds for every B > 0 (M8).

VACUITY GUARD (fmc-vacuity.py, ALL PASS):
- Changing the Coc exponent 2/27 to 1/27 makes A1/A2 FAIL.
- Making m_e independent of v makes A2 FAIL.
- With every Yukawa and alpha_s fixed, K_mu is nonzero (|K| > 0.5), so the narrowing really does come from the dropped hypotheses H-YUK-FIXED and H-AS-FIXED.

The non-tautological checks are not vacuous.

WHY REFUTED (grade only, not substance): the audit's OPEN rests solely on 'cannot be read here: alphaXiv quota exceeded'. That premise no longer holds. In this run, alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1009.5514 returned pages 1, 2, 23, 28, 51, 52, 54, 86, 88, 89, 91 and 99 of Uzan's review, which is the read the audit's own 'To NARROWED' clause asks for first. What those pages show:
- Only dimensionless combinations are constrained (Table 5, p.23; Table 10 and eq. 192, p.54/91).
- Finite bounds. QSO: 'mu is constant at the 10^-5 level during the past 11 Gigayrs' (p.52). NH3: |dmu/mu| < 1.8e-6 at z = 0.685 (2 sigma); HC3N: < 1.4e-6 at z = 0.89 (3 sigma) (p.52). Milky Way cloud vs lab: < 3e-8 (p.99). Clock: mu-dot/mu = (-3.8 +/- 5.6)e-14/yr (p.28, eq. 36).
- Model dependence. Eq. (184), p.88, is the Coc Lambda_QCD form with exponent 2/27, so A1 now attaches to a statement READ at source. The same page says 'the variation of Yukawa couplings, gauge couplings, Higgs vev and Lambda_QCD/M_P are correlated'. Literature translations to v explicitly 'assum[e] that the variation of the Yukawa couplings is negligible' (p.88) or that 'the Yukawa couplings are assumed constant' and the variation is 'homogeneous in space' (p.89). This confirms drift items B1-B4 and C1 as READ.
- Every measurement is made at a matter-bearing place, which confirms the sampled-places extrapolation.

Mapped through the audit's own D1 factors, these bounds give |dv/v| <= about 1.4e-5 (QSO), 2.6e-6 (NH3) and 4.3e-8 (Milky Way, H1, S = 0.0935), but only on H-YUK-FIXED + H1/H2 and only at the sampled places (fmc-uzan-bounds.out).

OVER-REPRESENTATION BOTH WAYS: the audit's sentence 'nothing computed or read here indicates any variation' must be amended. Uzan p.99 reports a measured cloud-lab offset dmu/mu = (2.2 +/- 0.4 stat +/- 0.3 sys)e-8 that 'could be interpreted as a variation of mu'. Earlier work gave k_mu ~ 1, which Uzan says 'may result from rest frequency uncertainties'. Table 10 lists 3.5 sigma H2 values (Ref. 425), where the authors 'do not claim for a detection' because systematics dominate. These are author-cautioned hints at matter-bearing places, not an accepted variation at unsourced places. They do not reach DATA-DEPENDENT or WRONG, but they belong in the record. Whether later work resolved the offset was NOT READ here.

GRADE: NARROWED. The constancy is real at the quoted finite bounds, but as support for P-UNIFORM it holds only on the hypotheses massform.py does not name at the site: H-YUK-FIXED, H-AS-FIXED (or address H1/H2), finite precision, and the extrapolation from sampled to unsourced places. There is no tree over-claim: status is PREMISE and no boolean asserts it. No D27, S10 or SR5 verdict moves.

Caveats:
- Uzan v1 dates from 2010. Lange 2010.06620 and later quasar/white-dwarf papers remain NAMED-NOT-READ, so the bounds quoted are a floor on what is known, not the current best.
- Every number above is quoted from the review's restatement of primary papers, not from the primary papers themselves.

audits.published_statement: NOT QUOTED, because the source was not read. The tree's form (branelink.py:38-39) is I_dot <= sqrt(pi P/(3 hbar))/ln 2 bits/s, i.e. S_dot <= sqrt(pi k^2 P/(3 hbar)). published_hypotheses: NOT QUOTED from the source, which was not read. The hypotheses under which this audit re-derived the form, each named:
H1: one channel is one transverse mode, with 1+1 propagation, unidirectional and without reflection.
H2: a free mode; energy is measured from the band bottom (or from mu for a Fermi sea); zero-point flux is excluded.
H3: the dispersion w(k) is monotone onto [0, inf). This is the 'field-blind' clause. A bounded band or a counted rest energy gives a strictly lower achievable ratio, so the ceiling still bounds.
H4: a stationary state, with information identified with entropy. This needs an ideal noiseless receiver, i.e. a Holevo capacity argument, which was not read.

verifiers.reason:
The audit graded OPEN for one reason only: neither Pendry nor any restatement could be reached. That reason no longer holds. The alphaXiv quota has reset, and I read both restatements at source this stage.

(1) Bekenstein & Schiffer, arXiv:quant-ph/0311050. This is now CONFIRMED as the arXiv copy of IJMPC 1 (1990) 355-422; its header prints that reference. It is also the tree's own second named source (branelink.py:40). Section 2.4, pp.6-7, restates Pendry's derivation, and eq.(16) reads 'I_max = (pi P/3 hbar)^{1/2} log2 e bits s^-1'. Sympy confirms it is identical to the tree's sqrt(pi P/(3 hbar))/ln 2, residual 0 (verify/refute/pendry_identity.py). The hypotheses are stated at source, and they match the audit's H1-H4 one for one:
- H1 is stated: one channel, uniform along the direction of propagation, modes labelled by p, a unidirectional current.
- H2/H3 are stated: 'assuming the energy spectrum is single valued and extends from 0 to inf. Then the form of the dispersion relation eps(p) does not enter.' The same section adds that the capacity is 'independent, not only of the form of the mode velocity v(eps), but also of its scale.' This is the 'field-blind' clause, READ.
- H4 is stated: 'The basic assumption is that I_max can be identified ... with the unidirectional thermodynamic entropy current', and the channel is noiseless.
- Massive bosons 'must be lower' (p.7). That matches the audit's check 3 (rest energy counted gives 0.9339 of the ceiling).
- Fermions give 'a capacity smaller by a factor sqrt 2. Pendry actually quotes the same capacity as for bosons ... because he considers the contributions of both particles and holes.' This matches the audit's check 4: the Fermi sea saturates the ceiling, and particles only reach 1/sqrt 2 of it.

(2) Blencowe & Vitelli, quant-ph/0001007v2. It quotes Pendry as 'S_dot^2/E_dot <= pi k_B^2/3 hbar ... obeyed for both bosons and fermions' (p.2). The bosonic optimum capacity in eq.(13) is (pi/ln2)sqrt(2P/3h), identical to the tree form (residual 0), and the paper gets it from Holevo's theorem via Caves-Drummond. That supplies H4 for bosons at source. The unidirectional fermion capacity in eq.(15) is 1/sqrt 2 of the ceiling, and bound (16) holds for all statistics g in [0,1].

I re-ran the audit's script: ALL PASS, exit 0. Its computations agree with both sources at every point where they overlap, so the computations are not where the grade fails.

By M's rule, the single-mode statement as the tree uses it is now READ through a restatement and machine-checked, so it is STANDS, not OPEN. Pendry 1983 itself stays NAMED-NOT-READ; it was read only as restated by Bekenstein-Schiffer and Blencowe-Vitelli.

Three things to record, none of them a refutation:
(a) Attribution. Bekenstein-Schiffer say the formula 'appeared in the earlier work of Lebedev and Levitin' (1963). That is a priority note, not an error in the result.
(b) Blencowe-Vitelli call the general-statistics, general-mu/T entropy bound (5) 'conjectured' and only tested numerically. The bosonic and Holevo case the tree uses is derived.
(c) Blencowe-Vitelli's journal is still unverified; the text printed none.

The tree's use beyond the hypotheses is a separate matter. Carrying the bound to a carrier with gamma > 1 on a moving brane in a 5D bulk is NARROWED: single mode only (sqrt(N), check 6), plus the uncomputed frame change for a massive carrier. But branelink.py:38-42 already refuses that use. The tree's tag 'NOT-FOUND (Pendry, Bekenstein & Schiffer not read)' is therefore now out of date for B&S, which has been read. That is recorded, not repaired.

verifiers.reason:
The grade stands. Under M's rule an unread source is OPEN, and the source was not read. The re-derivation supports the audit's conclusion, but three of the audit's supporting statements are wrong, unsupported or incomplete. They should be recorded as discrepancies, not repairs.

RE-RUN. I copied the script to verify/rederive/smcc.py and ran it. It prints ALL PASS and exits 0, but there are 26 PASS lines and 0 FAIL, not the "27 of 27" the audit reports. That is a miscount in the audit, not a physics finding.

ENCODING. Checks 1 to 4 encode the actual theorem: a per-channel 1+1 flux measured as dw/2pi, Bose and Fermi entropy, and dispersion independence through dk v_g = dw. They are not a toy. The audit proved maximality for every spectrum only through Lagrange plus concavity (checks 2a and 2b). Check 2c samples a narrow stretched-exponential family on a grid, and that grid reads 1.000147 for the thermal spectrum itself. I discharged the general case independently in indep.py V1 with a Legendre-dual proof: S - bP <= int dw/2pi [-ln(1-e^{-bw})] = pi/(12b) for any n(w). Minimising over b gives S <= sqrt(pi P/3) for every spectrum, so the single-mode theorem holds under H1-H4. The fermion dual gives the 1/sqrt 2 ceiling for particles only (V1d), which matches the audit's 4b' and 4c.

THREE CHECKS ARE CIRCULAR OR TAUTOLOGICAL.
- 5a defines the boosted flux as thermal at DT, then confirms that S scales by D.
- 5c is pure algebra over symbols: (DS)^2/(D^2 P) = S^2/P.
- 7 is an algebraic identity, which branelink.py:348 itself labels "proves nothing".
So the audit's Doppler-invariance evidence assumed its conclusion. The claim itself holds: my V4 computes it by quadrature for a non-thermal massless spectrum, using the invariant occupation and w' = Dw. The relative deviation is 3.5e-11 across D = 0.3, 2 and 7.

VACUITY GUARD.
- Mutating the ceiling constant from pi/3 to pi/6 makes 7 checks FAIL (mut1.py).
- Negating H1 breaks the ceiling: N thermal modes give N times pi/3 (V2, and the audit's own check 6).
So the checks are not vacuous.

NEW NARROWING OF THE AUDIT'S H3 TEXT. The audit says a failure of H3 (a bounded band, or a counted rest energy) "gives a strictly lower achievable ratio, so the ceiling still bounds". That is incomplete. A non-monotone single band, w = k^3 - 3k^2 + 2.5k, has forward branches that cover [0.364, 0.636] twice. It EXCEEDS the ceiling: the ratio is 1.0004 at T = 0.05, 1.016 at 0.1, 1.080 at 0.2, 1.156 at 0.5 and 1.127 at 2.0 (V3). "Field-blind" therefore holds per forward branch at each frequency, which is a Landauer channel, not per transverse mode. H3 must keep its monotone clause. Breaking H3 does not only lower the ratio.

A NAMED GAP PARTLY CLOSED. The audit lists the massive-carrier frame change as uncomputed. V5 takes a massive (m = 1) thermal right-moving flux and boosts it to rapidities 0, +-0.5 and +-1.5, measuring energy from the band bottom. The ratio is 1.0, 0.544, 0.384, 0.866 and 0.386: not invariant, but at or below 1 in every frame tested. The ceiling holds frame by frame because the dispersion keeps its form under the boost. This was tested only in 1+1 dimensions with a thermal source, so it is a finite check, not a general proof.

DATA. The hbar move of 8.0e-6 is confirmed (V6). The CODATA-1973 value is still the auditor's recollection, not read at source.

None of this lifts OPEN, because the source and its restatements are still unread. It also gives no ground for STANDS or WRONG of Pendry's text. The tree's refusal to apply the ceiling to a 5D-bulk carrier (branelink.py:38-42) gains support, since both multi-mode (V2) and non-monotone (V3) carriers exceed it.

audits.published_statement: CODATA 2018 recommended value: proton mass m_p = 1.672 621 923 69(51) x 10^-27 kg, relative standard uncertainty 3.0e-10 (READ via scipy txt2018 line 1454 and astropy codata2018.py:47). The current value (CODATA 2022) is m_p = 1.672 621 925 95(52) x 10^-27 kg (READ via scipy txt2022 line 1908; scipy's current set is 'CODATA 2022').
published_hypotheses: The value is the rest mass of one free proton (the table entry is 'proton mass'). It is not an average mass per nucleon or per baryon of bound matter.

The (51) is a one-standard-deviation standard uncertainty on an output of a least-squares adjustment, and the value is correlated with other adjusted constants. The table format was READ; the adjustment method is NAMED-NOT-READ.

In the tables m_p is not independent: m_p = A_r(p) m_u, with m_u = m_e/A_r(e) and m_e = 2hR_inf/(c alpha^2), where h and c are exact in the 2019 SI. This was verified numerically for both 2018 and 2022 in the rederive script, agreeing to 0.007 sigma and 0.042 sigma respectively.
A recommended value holds until the next adjustment supersedes it; the 2018 set was superseded by 2022.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, warpfolder.py:81 and :334-335 (printed at :401, pinned at :553): the tree treats m_p as the mass per baryon of 'ordinary matter' ('100 kg of ordinary matter is 5.98e28 baryons'; baryons_in = mass / M_PROTON). CODATA's m_p is the mass of a free proton. Computed from CODATA 2022 relative atomic masses, the mass per baryon is 1.007825 u for 1H atoms, 1.000651 u for 4He and 1.000000 u for 12C (exact by definition), against m_p = 1.007276 u. Counting every baryon at m_p undercounts 12C matter by 0.728% and 4He by 0.662%, and overcounts atomic H by 0.054%. So 100 kg of carbon is 6.02e28 baryons, not 5.98e28. The canonical entry names the hypothesis, but the sentence printed at warpfolder.py:81 does not carry it.

audits.lacked_data: Evidence for M's hypothesis: the 2018 authors did lack data that the 2022 adjustment had, and the value moved by +1.351e-9 relative, which is 4.43 of the 2018 standard uncertainties. The quoted 2018 uncertainty did not cover the move, so at the metrological level a recommended value can be off by more than its stated error. By the computed decomposition, essentially all of the move came through alpha, via m_p = A_r(p) m_e / A_r(e) with m_e = 2hR_inf/(c alpha^2); which measurements moved alpha was NOT read. Evidence against it mattering here: every tree quantity built on m_p (baryons_in, RHO_ISM, the magsail distances, and the copies in wavecorridor, gate1 and stock) moves by at most 3.6e-9 relative. That is at least five orders of magnitude below the tree's own tolerances (1e-3 and 1e-4), and it changes no refusal. The larger inaccuracy is not missing data but a hypothesis the tree added: using m_p as the mass per baryon of ordinary matter. That costs up to 0.73% and also changes no conclusion. The arrival.py prose-versus-computed discrepancy is internal to the tree and not caused by this datum.
audits.grade_evidence: As a measurement, the CODATA datum stands. The tree's literal is exactly the CODATA 2018 value, READ in two independent restatements, and it re-derives from its constituent constants to 0.007 sigma. Its 2022 replacement (+1.35e-9 relative, 4.4 sigma_2018, driven by alpha as computed) moves no tree number by more than 3.6e-9 and no conclusion at all. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS because the tree applies the datum to a wider class than it covers. warpfolder.py:81, 334-335, 401 and 553 count every baryon of 'ordinary matter' at the free-proton mass. That matches the printed 3 significant figures (5.98e28 per 100 kg) only for hydrogen-dominated matter. Computed from CODATA 2022, 100 kg of 12C holds 6.02e28 baryons (+0.728%) and 100 kg of 4He 6.02e28 (+0.662%). It is not WRONG: no refusal depends on the count (BLUEPRINT_SOURCES_BARYON_NUMBER = False is independent of it), and a sub-percent approximation is a discrepancy, not a refutation. Also recorded: arrival.py:25 truncates the 2018 value (-2.2e-9) with no source word. arrival.py:26-27 uses m_p as the ISM mean mass per particle, which is outside this datum and not audited. The prose at arrival.py:150-152 and 159 (810 AU, 2.6 ly) disagrees with the file's own computed 2002 AU and 0.084 ly; this discrepancy is not attributable to m_p. The source papers were never opened (alphaXiv quota, egress 403), so this audit rests on the NIST tables as scipy and astropy restate them.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the CODATA year and restates its use as baryons counted at the proton mass (hydrogen-like matter, up to +0.7% for heavier nuclei), or computes the count from atomic mass per nucleon. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a future adjustment moves m_p by more than about 1e-4 relative, the tree's tightest tolerance. That is five orders of magnitude beyond any historical CODATA move of m_p in the scipy tables (in units of e-27 kg: 1.672621637 in 2006, 1.672621777 in 2010, 1.672621898 in 2014, 1.67262192369 in 2018, 1.67262192595 in 2022). To OPEN: the NIST tables restated in scipy and astropy are shown to differ from the published CODATA papers; reading arXiv 2409.03787 and the 2018 RMP paper at source would settle this.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for codata-proton-mass, graded NARROWED
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the NARROWED grade in either direction. Three corrections to the audit's supporting text follow; none of them changes the grade.

(1) The source is now READ AT SOURCE. alphaXiv answered this time. The CODATA 2022 paper is arXiv 2409.03787v1, which confirms the id the audit only believed. Table XXXII (p.50) and Table XXXIII (p.53) print "proton mass m_p 1.672 621 925 95(52) x 10^-27 kg, 3.1e-10" and "1.007 276 466 5789(83) u". Both match the scipy restatement. The 2018 paper did not resolve on alphaXiv (a title query returned an unrelated paper, 2406.08293). So the 2018 value is still READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT only. The 2022 paper's Table XXXVIII (p.60) does corroborate the size of the move: alpha D_r = -4.5, m_u D_r = +4.6, m_e +4.5, mu_N -4.4, A_r(p) only -0.8. Section XVI.A (p.60-61) states that "the decrease in the recommended value of the fine-structure constant alpha by 4.5 times its 2018 uncertainty significantly influences" m_u = [2hR_inf/cA_r(e)] alpha^-2, and that "A_r(e) contributes negligibly". That confirms, at source, the audit's computed decomposition that alpha drove the shift and its 4.43 sigma_2018 figure (I recomputed 4.431).

(2) The lacked_data narrative needs a nuance READ at source (p.4 item 6). The move was not purely data the 2018 adjustment lacked. The 2011 h/m(87Rb) input used in 2018 had "previously unrecognized systematic effects", and the 2020 LKB value is "fractionally smaller by about 3 parts in 10^9" and supersedes it. New inputs also entered: a_e from NW-23 and Rb from LKB-20. Even so, the 2022 alpha data needed an expansion factor of 2.5 for inconsistency (p.61). So the evidence is "an input was wrong as well as missing", not only "lacked data". None of this moves any tree number.

(3) The audit's bound "up to 0.73%" understates the hypothesis drift. I recomputed it in verify/refute/codata-proton-mass-refute.py. For 100 kg of matter the true baryon count against the tree's 5.9786e28 is: 56Fe 6.029e28 (+0.845%), H2O 6.019e28 (+0.669%), 12C +0.728%, 4He +0.662%, a cosmic H/He mix with X=0.75 +0.125% (5.99e28), and atomic 1H -0.054%. The printed 3-sig-fig "5.98e28 for 100 kg of ordinary matter" therefore holds only for nearly pure hydrogen or free protons. It does not hold for any terrestrial matter, and it does not hold even for the primordial mix. That strengthens the NARROWED finding rather than undermining it. The maximum is about 0.85%, near the iron peak, not 0.73%.

Why it is not WRONG: no refusal depends on the count. BLUEPRINT_SOURCES_BARYON_NUMBER = False is independent of it. A sub-percent approximation is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

Why it is not STANDS: the tree's added hypothesis (every baryon of ordinary matter counted at the free-proton mass) is outside what CODATA's datum covers, and it visibly changes the printed figure at the precision printed.

Other checks reproduced: the rederive script exits 0 with REDERIVE OK; warpfolder.py --selftest passes its baryon pins (5.978637e28); arrival.py prints 2002 AU and 0.08 ly against prose of 810 AU and 2.6 ly. That confirms the audit's in-passing discrepancy, and it is not attributable to m_p. The arrival.py:25 truncation (-2.2e-9) is confirmed, and so is its reuse in gate1, stock and stockgate.

audits.published_statement: HPS p.8: 'for sufficiently large l ... f(l) = F(l) + phi(l); r(l) = R(l) + rho(l), where F(l) and R(l) are strictly monotone increasing and phi(l) and rho(l) are bounded oscillating functions ... in the limit of large l, R(l) ~ l and F(l) ~ (a ln l - b)^2 for a = 5.3 and b = 25.5. From these combined numeric and analytic calculations we see that for the chosen set of boundary conditions, R(l) -> l, thus our self-consistent wormhole connects two spatial regions which are asymptotically flat, modulo the Planck-scale wiggles. The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the metric is static and spherically symmetric, ds^2 = -f dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 (eq. (2)).

H2: the source is the AHS analytic approximation for a massless, zero-temperature, conformally coupled (xi = 1/6) scalar, with mu absorbed into f (eqs. (4)-(7), fn [20]); G = 8 pi <T>, K^2 = 1/(5760 pi).

H3: 'for the chosen set of boundary conditions' means eq. (9) data and the ONE displayed solution, ln f(0) = -2/3. The statement does not cover the whole family, or the other solutions mentioned on p.8.

H4: F ~ (a ln l - b)^2 comes from 'combined numeric and analytic calculations', guided by the numerics, and the fitting range is not stated. The l -> infinity conclusion is therefore an extrapolation.
H5: 'asymptotically flat' is used to mean that f approaches a constant. The spatial part is called asymptotically flat 'modulo the Planck-scale wiggles'. No formal definition is given.
H6: HPS do not say which system they integrated. The tree records HPS_INTEGRATED_THE_PRINTED_SYSTEM = 'NOT DETERMINED' (hpscentre.py:279).
hypothesis_drift: NONE on the owner line. hpscentre.py:99-101 says 'For the throat the failure is HPS's own statement ... plus the measurement'. Here 'the throat' means section (d)'s eq. (9) data with ln f(0) = -2/3 (hpscentre.py:76-77, :246), which is HPS's H3. The quotation is verbatim, and the tree does not call the statement a theorem.

WORDING, in the ledger summary and not in the owner file: canonical.json gives the hypothesis as 'HPS's own throat solutions', in the plural. HPS's statement is about one displayed solution (H3). Reading the ledger row as covering the whole family -1 <= ln f(0) < 0 would add scope that HPS do not state.

TRANSFER, named by the tree and not dropped: HPS's sentence is about HPS's own trajectory, whose system is NOT DETERMINED (hpscentre.py:279, :311-318). The tree applies it to its CONSERVED-reading trajectory from the same data (hpscentre.py:76-82), and the transfer rests on 'plus the measurement'. Part B of this audit finds the non-flatness in BOTH readings, so the open which-system question does not move this conclusion.

DEFINITION: the tree uses the statement as a failure of Popov's asymptotic-flatness hypothesis (hpscentre.py:94-96, DOMAIN_WORD :299-301). This audit did not read Popov's definition (hep-th/0302039 is NAMED-NOT-READ here). The failure does not depend on which definition is used: an unbounded f and a Komar integral that grows linearly fail any definition that needs a normalisable static Killing field with finite mass. This rests on a named hypothesis that was not machine-checked: d/dt is the static Killing field, unique up to scale.

Part A, exact (sympy):
- A1: (5.3 ln l - 25.5)^2 -> oo, and lam^2 F -> oo for every lam, so no normalisation of t makes f -> 1. The divergence holds for every a != 0, and a = 0 is the only member of the family with f constant. Recorded: the law vanishes at l0 = e^{b/a} = 122.9, and omega_2^2 is singular on (111.6, 135.4), so the law only holds at large l.
- A2: on the smooth part (r = l, f = F), G^t_t = 0 = G^th_th and G^l_l = 2a/(l^2 (a ln l - b)); the conservation identity closes.
- A3: the Komar integral is M_K = r^2 f'/(2 sqrt f) = a l, which diverges under every rescaling of t. Control: Schwarzschild gives M_K = M.
- A4: the AHS source (conserved reading), evaluated on the smooth part alone, is 8.1e-5, 1.7e-6 and 2.2e-8 of G^l_l at 1e3, 1e4 and 1e5 K. So the smooth law is not self-consistent by itself; the ripples carry the growth. This is recorded, not graded.

audits.lacked_data:
What HPS had: an integration over an unstated range, and an asymptotic analysis guided by that integration.

What they lacked:
(i) The conservation test. It selects the one conserved reading of the three places where the HPS and Popov printings disagree, so HPS may have integrated a non-conserved system.
(ii) Popov 2003's statement that the AHS approximation is established for asymptotically flat spacetimes.
(iii) Long-range integrations.

Evidence: (i) and (iii) do NOT change the conclusion. In both readings f grows with no sign of saturation: <sqrt f> goes from 6.0 to 45.9 (conserved) and from 6.8 to 36.5 (printed-M1) between 300 and 9.9e4 K. The local slope is still rising at 8e4 K, and the Komar integral grows linearly. The fitted a moves with the window (4.7-8.9), but the conclusion only needs a != 0. (ii) changes how the tree uses the statement, not whether it holds.

What remains: only behaviour beyond 1e5 K. The l -> infinity claim is an extrapolation for HPS and for this audit alike (H4), and nothing points to saturation. M's hypothesis is therefore not borne out for this result: the data HPS lacked confirm it, and Hochberg-Visser 1998 states it more strongly.

(9), ln f(0) = -2/3) and names the added support ('plus the measurement'). No hypothesis is dropped or weakened on the owner line; the only drift is the ledger summary's plural 'solutions'.
2. The exact re-derivation agrees: the printed law diverges for every a != 0 and every normalisation of t, and its Komar integral grows as a l, against the finite Schwarzschild control.
3. The measurement agrees, independently of which system HPS integrated: in both readings from eq. (9) data, integrated to 1e5 K, <sqrt f> strictly increases by more than 5x and <M_K>/x stays flat within 3x, where a finite mass would make it fall 330x.
4. No moved datum moves the conclusion: (a, b) depend on the fitting window, but only a != 0 matters, and a > 4.6 in every window.

Limits named with the grade:
- The l -> infinity claim is an extrapolation beyond 1e5 K (H4), the same limit HPS's own claim has.
- d/dt is taken as the static Killing field.
- Popov's definition of asymptotic flatness was not re-read.

Recorded, not graded: the smooth law is not self-consistent without the ripples (A4). The spatial ripples are of order one to 1e5 K, which conflicts with HPS's 'modulo the Planck-scale wiggles' and fits Hochberg-Visser 1998. That is a discrepancy between two printings, not a refutation.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
NARROWED: an analysis, or an integration well beyond 1e5 K, showing that the ripple-averaged source falls faster than 1/l^2, so that f saturates and the Komar integral converges for some reading or some eq. (9) data. Or a reading of Popov's definition that such a metric nevertheless meets.
OPEN: evidence that the text layer misstates p.8, for example if the PRL typesetting differs.
DATA-DEPENDENT: a window or reading in which the fitted a approaches 0.

1. Source, read myself. The audit's own alphaXiv calls had failed on quota; mine worked. answer_pdf_queries(gr-qc/9701064) returned the arXiv v1 text layer, all 12 pages. p.8 says verbatim: 'The redshift function however, does not approach a constant value as l -> infinity, so the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat'. The same sentence gives F ~ (a ln l - b)^2 with a = 5.3, b = 25.5, and the scope 'for the chosen set of boundary conditions'. p.7 gives eq. (9) and the one displayed solution, ln f(0) = -2/3. The tree's quotation (hpscentre.py:100) and the audit's quotation are both verbatim. The abstract ('connecting two asymptotically spatially flat regions') fits p.8's split: the spatial part is called flat, the full metric is not. No misreading, and no reliance on a restatement.

2. Later literature, also read myself. alphaXiv returned gr-qc/9802046v2 p.3. It calls HPS 'joining up two spacetimes with no asymptotically flat spatial regions' and cites PRL 78, 2050 as ref. [7]. The audit records this correctly: it is a stronger claim than HPS p.8 and a discrepancy between two printings, not a refutation of the one being graded. It strengthens the non-flatness, if anything.

3. Hypothesis drift. The owner line (hpscentre.py:99-101, 'For the throat ... HPS's own statement ... plus the measurement') uses the statement for the same eq. (9) / ln f(0) = -2/3 solution HPS state it for, and names its added support. The only drift is the plural 'solutions' in the canonical.json ledger row. The audit already flags that wording, and the owner file does not carry it. So no drift undermines STANDS.

4. Computations, re-derived independently in verify/refute/notaf_check.py. On r = l, f = (a ln l - b)^2:
- G^t_t = 0 and G^th_th = 0.
- G^l_l = 2a/(l^2 (a ln l - b)).
- The Komar integral r^2 f'/(2 sqrt f) = a l.
- (5.3 ln l - 25.5)^2 -> oo.
- The zero of the law is at l0 = e^{b/a} = 122.894.
All of these match the audit's A1-A3. I read gr-qc_9701064_not-af.out: ALL PASS, exit 0. Its Part B numbers say what the audit says:
- <sqrt f> rises 6.02 -> 45.91 (conserved reading) and 6.84 -> 36.50 (printed-M1 reading).
- <M_K>/x stays in the range 9.1-12.1 and 7.0-5.0, i.e. flat, not falling.

So the non-flatness holds in both readings of the system HPS might have integrated, and the open which-system question (HPS_INTEGRATED_THE_PRINTED_SYSTEM = NOT DETERMINED) does not move it.

5. Moved data. a and b depend on the fitting window: 4.7-8.9 and 20-57. Divergence only needs a != 0, so none of this moves the conclusion. Over-representation in M's favour is also avoided: the audit records the A4 finding (the smooth law is not self-consistent without the ripples) and the order-one spatial ripples as recorded-not-graded, rather than calling them HPS errors.

6. The strongest downward case is H4: the l -> infinity statement is an extrapolation and cannot be checked strictly at finite range. Under M's rule that pushes towards OPEN. But two things hold:
- The tree uses the result only as 'HPS's own statement plus the measurement', and both halves are accurate.
- The audit names the extrapolation beyond 1e5 K as a limit attached to the grade. That limit is shared with HPS's own claim, and nothing measured points to saturation.
Grading the READ statement STANDS with that named limit is not over-representation.

Residual notes, which do not change the grade:

- d/dt as the unique static Killing field is a named hypothesis that was not machine-checked.
- The later_literature 'contested' value on the NOT-READ search entry is a schema placeholder, as the audit itself says, and must not be read as a contesting paper.

RE-RUN. I copied gr-qc_9701064_not-af.py and _hps_tree into verify/rederive/notaf/ and ran it with argument 1e5. It exited 0 with SUMMARY: ALL PASS. All three C0 md5 checks matched the live tree. The source sentence at hps_0.xml:1183-1185 matches the quoted statement verbatim.

ENCODING. Part A is a toy of the fit, not of the solution. A1, A3a and A3b only show that HPS's own fitted law (a ln l - b)^2 diverges, and that its Komar integral is a*l. That is true of the fit, and on its own it does not touch the trajectory. The physics conclusion rests on Part B, which re-integrates the tree's 4th-order system from eq. (9) data. Part B is the right object for HPS's statement, which concerns one solution (H3). The Komar formula r^2 f'/(2 sqrt f) is correct in proper-length gauge. I checked by hand the Schwarzschild control that A3c returns (M_K = M).

CONVERGENCE (my conv.py, to 1e4 K, rtol 1e-8, 1e-10 and 1e-12). In both readings, <sqrt f> and <M_K>/x agree to all printed digits, so the growth is not a tolerance artefact. In the conserved reading, the unenforced ll constraint holds to a relative 1e-7, 1e-9 and 1e-11 respectively, so that trajectory is a genuine solution of its system.

QUALIFICATION 1, not a refutation. The printed-M1 trajectory violates its own ll equation at relative 2.0, 1.1, 0.66 and 0.44 at 300, 1e3, 3e3 and 9.9e3 K, at every rtol. It is therefore not a solution of the full printed-M1 system. The audit's claim that 'Part B finds the non-flatness in BOTH readings, so the which-system question does not move this conclusion' should be narrowed. It should read: the conserved reading is a solution; printed-M1 is the trajectory a tt+thth integration of the printed system produces, and that trajectory fails ll at order one. verifiers.reason:
The audit gives four grounds for NARROWED. Checked against sources read this pass, none of them narrows the external result as the tree uses it.

(iii) 'running continuously' is misread. The audit says this clause "needs a decay rate" and cites Jitomirskaya-Liu. I READ arXiv:1805.01072v2 at source through alphaXiv. Its Theorems 1.1, 3.1 and 3.2 build asymptotically flat manifolds that carry embedded eigenvalues. In their sense, asymptotically flat means radial curvature K(r) -> 0 at any rate, and their examples have K_rad = O(1/r). Even those manifolds have sigma_ess(-Delta) = sigma_ac(-Delta) = [0,oo). So the absolutely continuous spectrum still runs all the way down to zero. What fails without a decay rate is purity, meaning no eigenvalues embedded in that spectrum. The tree's wording, "spectrum running continuously down to zero", never claims purity. J-L p.2 also restates Kumura, Donnelly and Garofalo [5,7,16]: there are no positive eigenvalues when K_rad = o(r^-2). Those papers are NAMED-NOT-READ, restated only. On the corridor, concentric.py:164 gives Phi = m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/r for r > R_s, which is about -m a^2/(2 r^3). Curvature therefore falls off like r^-5, so even the strict "purely continuous" reading is covered on the corridor through that restatement.

(iv) The literature is no longer unread. I READ Charalambous & Lu, arXiv:1211.3225v2, at source.
- p.1: -Delta is nonnegative, so sigma is contained in [0,oo).
- p.5, Theorem 2.1: the classical Weyl criterion, with the weakly-null condition that places a point in sigma_ess.
- p.4, Theorem 1.3: with radial Ricci curvature asymptotically nonnegative, the L^2 spectrum is [0,oo).
- p.2: completeness is not needed for the criterion itself.
This confirms, at source, the audit's own Weyl-sequence proof of inf spec = 0. Donnelly 1999 is still NAMED-NOT-READ; both papers cite it.

(ii) The (5.6) scope point belongs to another key. The narrowing of "(5.6) returns the flat bound exactly" to the formula's Minkowski and open-RW derivation is about F&T (5.6). canonical.json has a separate key for it, fewster-teo-5.6-spectral-gap-bound, whose statement_as_used covers fewsterteo.py:70-103 with hypotheses "ultrastatic, H^3" and "lower limit C = spectral gap". Using it here counts the same drift against two keys.

(i) Massless and minimal coupling are not narrowings of the theorem. "Laplace spectrum" has no mass and no potential by definition. Whether the field's w^2 operator is that Laplacian is a question about how the tree applies the theorem. The audit concedes the tree's model satisfies both conditions, so this is drift to record, not a narrower theorem. The one real gap between the theorem's literal statement and its use is the operator. The corridor is static rather than ultrastatic, so the relevant operator is K, not Delta_h. The audit's own S3 measures K by the same Weyl argument: quotients 3.08/w^2 -> 0, residual 1.414/L, all checks PASS when I re-ran the script (exit 0). So the use extends the theorem to K, and that extension is computed to hold. Nothing has to be cut back.

What survives as findings, none of which moves a grade:
- The theorem's wording omits "massless, minimally coupled". This is drift, and it is satisfied.
- The Laplace vs K identification is drift, and the extension is computed.
- The cavity C = 0.005 is called "most generous", but the Dirichlet gap is pi/200. This is a DISCREPANCY in wording only.

One small inaccuracy in the audit, which moves nothing: it calls the corridor slice "smooth". max(r,R_s) at concentric.py:164 leaves a kink at the shell, so the metric is Lipschitz with a thin shell. This is a compact perturbation; Weyl sequences far out in the r^-3 end are unaffected, and so are inf spec = 0 and sigma_ess = [0,oo).

On a sourced reading, the clause the tree relies on holds, under hypotheses the corridor meets: spectrum = [0,oo), w_min = 0. Every conclusion stays unmoved: 71.256 STANDS, 72.599 and 72.247 stay REFUSED, O2 stays OPEN. So the grade should be STANDS, with the drift items recorded and not repaired. NARROWED counts against the tree on two grounds that do not hold up: a "continuously" claim that J-L, read at source, contradicts, and a (5.6) drift that belongs to a sibling key.

Radial test functions are legitimate: they give the upper bounds, and with K >= 0 that is enough. I checked the quadratic-form weights in both RECONSTRUCTED forms by hand: N sqrt(h) h^rr against sqrt(h)/N for K, and sqrt(h) h^rr against sqrt(h) for Delta_h. All four are right.

Three weaknesses, none fatal:
(a) The S3 'every quotient > 0' checks are tautological. A quotient of positive weights cannot be negative, and S3 never includes a potential term.
(b) At widths >= 1e2, S3 samples only the region where Phi ~ -1e-13 (vacuity.py V0). There the corridor is flat to that level, so S3 is the flat computation again. Only the width-10 sample (5.6e-4 off flat) and the core-straddling test touch non-flat geometry. That is the theorem's own mechanism (far-out test functions), but S3 adds little independent evidence beyond S2.
(c) The 'massive field' check is only inf N^2 > 0. No spectrum with a mass term was computed.

- V1, mass hypothesis negated (mu = 0.1): the same quotients go to 0.0100000 = mu^2, so S3's 'quotient < 1e-8' criterion fails. Masslessness is load-bearing and the check can detect its absence.

Conformal coupling (xi = 1/6) does not bind. The audit's hedged 'could bind' is therefore true only for large xi, which narrows that drift note further.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported by items (i) and (ii) and by the operator drift. (i) The tree's sentence never states 'massless, minimally coupled', though its model satisfies both. (ii) (5.6) is READ as derived only for Minkowski and open RW, so 'returns the flat bound exactly' holds for the formula, not for F&T's bound on the corridor.

One caution against over-representation in that NARROWED. Item (iii), "'continuously' needs an unstated decay hypothesis", rests on reading 'running continuously' as 'purely continuous spectrum'. Under the plain set reading, sigma = [0,oo) with no gap, the audit's own Weyl-sequence argument proves the clause. The only condition needed is that the metric tends to Euclidean (with first derivatives) on balls far out, and embedded eigenvalues do not open a gap. Item (iii) should be recorded as a reading choice, not as evidence for NARROWED.

The cavity 'most generous' C=0.005 against Dirichlet pi/200 is correctly marked a DISCREPANCY and moves nothing. NARROWED stands, though the audit has three errors, none load-bearing.

**Sources.** I re-read both papers live through alphaXiv (the quota was available again): 2503.14738v3 pp.20, 22-25, 28 and 33, and 2511.07526v1 pp.1-6. The audit's load-bearing quotes match the source:

- Significance over LCDM: 3.1, 2.8, 3.8 and 4.2 sigma.
- p.33 says "phantom crossing at some point in the past (in this parametrization)".
- Caldwell-Linder say "no violation of the NEC takes place, past or future" and that the energy conditions "do not apply separately to individual components". The Fig.3 caption prints "w_a ≈ 1" where the text prints "w_a ≈ −1". The audit correctly records this as a misprint, not a refutation.

**Owner lines.** I re-read achievable.py:49-53, 435-442 and 549-553. The tree states "DARK ENERGY has negative PRESSURE and POSITIVE energy density. rho_Lambda > 0" with no hypothesis on w. NOT_EXCEPTIONS does have 3 entries under a "TWO THINGS" heading.

**Computation.** I re-ran the rederive script; it exits 0. Independently, I reproduced:
- the CPL crossing redshifts: 0.354, 0.405, 0.440, 0.496;
- the boost needed at z=1 for a boosted observer to see rho_DE < 0: gamma = 2.10-2.79, from gamma^2 > w/(1+w).

The logic holds. For a perfect fluid, rho[gamma^2(1+w) - w] ≥ 0 for every observer iff w ≥ -1. The tree's claim is about "dark energy" in general but its argument is the w = -1 case, so it drops the hypothesis w_de ≥ -1. That is a narrowing of scope.

**Why not STANDS.** The tree's conclusion is "the wrong sign of the wrong quantity". For a phantom component, rho + p < 0, and that is the kind of energy-condition violation the board needs. So the dropped hypothesis matters for the claim's purpose, not only for its wording.

**Why not WRONG.** In every Table V row, Omega_DE > 0 in the comoving frame. Following Caldwell-Linder's own reading, the total fluid never violates the NEC.

**Why not DATA-DEPENDENT.** The phantom preference is below 5 sigma and depends on which SNe sample is used. The board's use of the claim also does not move with any datum read: the effect is about 56 orders of magnitude short of the density the tree needs.

**Discrepancies in the audit (recorded, not grade-moving):**
1. The audit says Omega_DE is "0.647-0.707 in all DESI Table V models". Over every Table V row, 1 - Omega_m - Omega_K actually runs from 0.645 (w0waCDM+Omega_K, DESI alone) to 0.797 (wCDM, CMB alone). The sign is positive throughout.
2. The audit leans on "in this parametrization" (p.33), lists the phantom episode as parametrization-dependent, and names "independent of the parametrization" as a condition not yet met. But DESI p.25, read at source, says the phantom crossing "and the consequent violation of the NEC, is thus rather independent of parametrization choices", backed by binned reconstruction (Fig.12). It adds the caveat that w is not directly observable and that NEC-respecting models can be built. So the audit understates DESI's own claim. Correcting this strengthens NARROWED, not STANDS, and does not reach DATA-DEPENDENT for the reasons above.
3. DESI (pp.23 and 25) calls component phantom behaviour an NEC violation; Caldwell-Linder say the NEC applies only to the total fluid. The audit presents only the Caldwell-Linder side. This is a disagreement between the sources over what the term covers, and it should be recorded as such.

audits.name: Topology: R^3 is simply connected and a wormhole spatial section is not; no continuous metric deformation on a fixed manifold changes topology

source.located: No single source: the tree cites none. create.py:24-26 and phase1.py:50-52 state it without a citation. The mathematics is standard algebraic topology (pi_1(R^3)=1; pi_1(S^1xS^2)=Z; a family of metrics on a fixed manifold leaves the manifold unchanged), and it is re-derived here. How the literature applies it to WORMHOLES was read in three places. (a) Hochberg & Visser, arXiv:gr-qc/9704082v1 (1997), abstract and sec. 1. (b) Pisana, Shoshany, Antoniou, Kauffman, Lambropoulou, arXiv:2505.02210v4, the paper create.py:125 cites: sec. I.A, sec. II (the 0-surgery list), sec. III.A (Def. 6, Thm III.1-III.2) and sec. III.D. (c) Borde, arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, sec. IX.C.

audits.published_statement:
No source publishes the tree's sentence as such. What the sources read here say:
2505.02210 sec. II: '3-dimensional 0-surgery: An embedding of S^0 x D^3 is replaced by D^1 x S^2 ... This surgery corresponds to the creation of a wormhole'.
2505.02210 sec. I.A: 'wormholes: handles attached to spacetime'. The same section restates Geroch: 'if the two 3-manifolds are non-homeomorphic, Geroch's second theorem requires that the spacetime contains either singularities or closed timelike curves'.
2505.02210 sec. III.D: 'all the "topological charge" is confined within a compact region'.
2505.02210 Def. 6: a spacetime carries 'an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'.
Hochberg-Visser, abstract: 'topology is too limited a tool to accurately characterize a generic traversable wormhole: in general one needs geometric information ... we shall define the wormhole throat in terms of a 2-dimensional constant-time hypersurface of minimal area'.
Hochberg-Visser, sec. 1: the 'Morris-Thorne class of inter-universe traversable wormholes' requires 'two asymptotically flat regions'. The same section says there are wormholes with 'trivial topology', for example 'a single closed Friedman-Robertson-Walker spacetime connected by a narrow neck to ordinary Minkowski space'.
Borde IX.C: 'Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed.'
published_hypotheses: (math) The manifold is FIXED across the family, and each g_s is a nondegenerate metric on it for every s in the CLOSED interval [0,1]. Under that hypothesis the topology cannot change, by definition.
(math) 'Wormhole' means a manifold carrying a 1-handle: R^3 # (S^1xS^2), the result of 3-dimensional 0-surgery (2505.02210 sec. II). Its pi_1 is Z.

(Hochberg-Visser) A wormhole is defined geometrically, by a throat: a constant-time 2-surface of minimal area with flare-out. Under this definition wormholes with trivial topology exist, and the Morris-Thorne inter-universe wormholes have two ends.

(2505.02210 / Geroch as restated) A topology change needs a cobordism that is not a product. For a nondegenerate, time-orientable Lorentzian metric that means CTCs or singularities. The change can be confined to a compact region.
(Borde IX.C) Degenerate metrics at isolated points allow spacetimes that change topology. This lies outside 'nondegenerate g_s on a fixed manifold'.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: the restriction to handle wormholes (intra-universe, not simply connected). create.py:24, the create.py:153 docstring, the create.py:325-326 verdict and phase1.py:50-51 all say 'a wormhole is not [simply connected]' with no qualifier. Two counterexamples, computed here: the Morris-Thorne inter-universe section R x S^2 IS simply connected (C3), and a Hochberg-Visser trivial-topology wormhole has R^3 itself as its section. The restriction is kept where the claim bears load: specthm.py:63 and specthm.py:731 ('A shortcut through non-simply-connected spatial topology'). For R x S^2 the tree's conclusion still holds, but through H_2 = Z (two ends), not through simple connectivity.

WIDENED: 'throat' used where the claim only holds for a 'handle'. Sites: phase1.py:57-58 'CREATING a throat is a TOPOLOGY problem', create.py:41-42 'CREATE bring a throat into existence ... A TOPOLOGY problem', and the canonical merged name 'cannot produce a throat'. Under Hochberg-Visser's definition this is false. C4 builds a smooth metric family on FIXED R^3 that is unchanged outside 1<r<3 and still acquires a minimal 2-sphere with flare-out (R'=0 and R''=14.2>0 at r=1.993) from s* ~ 0.277 onward. What needs a topology change is a handle or a second end, not a throat. The throat built here opens into a bounded region, not onto a shortcut, so it is not a gate.

MIS-ATTRIBUTED (a discrepancy inside the tree, not a refutation). create.py:15-16 assigns the FIXED MANIFOLD clause to D1, while phase1.py:16-17 places it in the definition's preamble. The table at create.py:18-19 and the code at create.py:138 hard-code D1 YES and D2 NO. C5 computes that the handle's topology change is confined to a ball, matching 2505.02210 III.D. So the handle does not violate compact support (D2); it violates the fixed-manifold clause. The conclusion that the gate is not a phase1 transition is unaffected.

IMPLICIT, NOW NAMED: g_s must be nondegenerate at every s in the closed interval [0,1]. The phrase 'at ANY support' at create.py:24-26 is exact only under this hypothesis. The escapes lie outside it: Borde IX.C (Horowitz) and 2505.02210 I.A (degenerate metrics, Morse singularities).

HARD-CODED: fails_on_topology() at create.py:152-155 returns the literal True, and the check at create.py:271 compares that literal with True. That is a restatement, not a computation. This audit's C2 and C5 provide the computation for the handle class.

data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: There is no datum to move. The only empirical premise is that the background is spatially R^3. C6 shows the handle conclusion does not depend on it: H_1(T^3 # S^1xS^2) = Z^4, not Z^3, so adding a handle changes any closed background.

The claim stands for the class the tree's load-bearing site names. A spatial section with a handle, which is not simply connected, cannot arise from R^3 through any nondegenerate metric family on the fixed manifold, whatever the support (computed in C1, C2, C5 and C6; 2505.02210 READ).
